Kevin MacLeod – His royalty free music Lithium, Mystery, The Pyre, Midnight Tales, Skye Cuillin, Frozen Star Freesound Community – Terror Scream sound effect Universfield – Crowd Disappointment sound effect Kidjoker27 on Deviant Art – The Omniscient Grimoire artwork. Slingers – for many artworks we shared. Summary Caster of Magic Warlord mod's main goal is to improve immersion and reduce repetition when using normal military units. Normal units have been redesigned, and several dozen new stock and racial unique units (with complete new animated sprites) have been added across the board. The units recruited from Armorer's Guild and Fantastic Stable buildings typically cost more and are far more advanced than their Caster of Magic counterparts. These units are not part of the Caster of Magic design of being disposable and inferior to summons and spammed all over the world to the point of clutter. Four new races have also been introduced – Xuanyuan, Hawkmen, Rakhshasa, and Goblin The mod also considers asymmetric game balance to be a key factor to game enjoyment to stay true to the spirit of Master of Magic. There will be moments where you might wonder an individual element is unusually strong – for the most part that is intentional though minor balancing tweaks will continue with future versions. There have been spell modifications, including entirely new summon units. Two additional uncommon (total 12) and three rare tier spells (total 18) are available for research. Realms have been re-balanced accordingly and magic realm themes have been preserved. Gold and food maintenance of units have been adjusted to lessen unit spam, particularly for AI wizards. Economic buildings with lower upkeep to prevent them being a drain to your coffers (only your military and rush- buying should be). Races, heroes, and building mechanics have also been redesigned to fit the modder vision, then heavily play- tested with balance taken into consideration. Some of these updates reverse changes from Caster of Magic to something closer to the original Master of Magic, albeit not completely. There are also visual changes. Additional changes across the board are for you to discover. Many are not included in this manual as they are not related to gameplay, just immersion.
PDF page 2 Installation How to install (1.5.12.6): 1) Uninstall/unload old version of mod (see below) **** 2) Create folder “Master of Magic Caster Windows 1.5.11”. 3) Copy all content inside folder “Master of Magic Caster Windows” to “Master of Magic Caster Windows 1.5.11” 4) Install patch of Caster of Magic for windows version 1.5.11 (which could be found here: https://www.realmsbeyond.net/forums/showthread.php?tid=11090 ) by copy content from folder “CoMWin1511” inside the zip file into folder “Master of Magic Caster Windows 1.5.11”. 5) Unpack "CoM2ModWarlord1.5.12.6.7z" into "...\Master of Magic Caster Windows 1.5.11\Mods" folder. 6) Run caster of magic for windows 1.5.11 from folder “Master of Magic Caster Windows 1.5.11” until reach main menu. 7) Choose the "Load Mod" option in the lower right corner. 8) Type mod name "WARLORD" and enter. This will automatically load mod files into the data folder while original file in data folder would be backup for sake of later reversion. (In case you have your own customize artifact, backup your own "items.dat" before doing so or you would lose them.) 9) Once the process is completed, game will automatically exit. 10) Run caster of magic for windows again, now game would become Caster of Magic for Windows: Warlord. 11) Please play the game with these setting… - Pick “Use Legacy Tileset” (to activate Civizard tileset) - Pick “Remove Tree” (so that tree in combat would not be too messy) How to reset environments setting back to original (tile back to legacy tileset, raise volcano animation, combat vegetation and combat item as well as music back to original) 1) Copy content in folder “mods\Warlord\backup original environment\” to “data” folder. 2) Now you are free to pick “Remove Tree” or not pick “Use Legacy Tileset” setting. How to reset music back to original only. 1) Copy content in folder “mods\Warlord\backup original environment\music” to “data\music” folder. How to uninstall the mod. 1) Go to the main menu. 2) Click "Unload Mod" option on lower right corner. Game will automatically unload the mod and replacing them with backup files (not included your own items in "items.dat", this one must be done by yourself) 3) Game would exit upon completing process. 4) Restart the game and game would be back to become original Caster of Magic for Windows without Warlord mod.
PDF page 3 Book System and Retorts has been modified: • How many spells are granted per book. The new system is fully symmetrical (1-3-4-5-6-7-8-10) • being able to research a single common-tier spell at random for all realms without books chosen. • Starting Power Changed. Every book always grants starting power and skill, not just when you have 4+ books of a type. Book 3 to Book 4 no longer grants +6 starting power. • Starting Power Formula is now 9 + 1 for books 1-7 + 2 for books 8-9 + 3 for books 10-11 and +4 for book 12 • Starting skill follows fairly closely, though due to different method of calculation may be slightly lower for first 3 books of a type. • Guaranteed very rares eliminated • Guaranteed rares limited to book 10 only (as guaranteed early rare) • Book-based discounts changed from 8% research / 5% spell per book starting book #9 to 5% research (starting book #6) and 3% (starting book #7) • Books 9 and 10 grant an additional starting common spell. The amount of starting overland skill is approximately 2 to 4 below Caster of Magic (reduction of 1 per 3 books) to balance city vs magic production early in the game (given the changes that took place in city mechanics) Book Common Uncommon Rare* V. PDF page 4 Retorts Retorts have been reworked with some retorts change, all of them get spells exclusive to their own. Alchemy Alchemist: The wizard is an expert in the art of Alchemy. • Allows the wizard to convert gold to mana and mana to gold at a rate of 1:1. • All non-summoned units trained by the wizard from non-Barbarian cities gain magic weapons. • Alchemist's Guild cost 15% cheaper. • Could access to spell “Philosopher’s Stone”. • Costs 2 picks. Warlord: The wizard is a renowned militarist. • All non-summoned units under the wizard's control have their veterancy level increased by one. • Allows non-summoned units to exceed their normal veterancy limit by one level. • Barracks, War College, Armory, Fighter's Guild, Armorer's Guild, City Wall, Fortification, Hillfort, and Warlord's Hold cost 15% cheaper. • Warlord could utilize global ability of Warlord's Hold regardless of home race. • Could access to spell “Wall of Stone”. • Could access to spell “Mark of Conqueror”. • Mutually exclusive with the Tactician retort at the start of the game. • Costs 2 picks. Channeler: The wizard has mastered the art of channeling spellcraft. • Allows the wizard to cast spells without range penalties. • Reduces spell range penalties during banishment by half. • Reduces overall spell upkeep by 50%. • Reduces the cost of casting spells in combat by 12%. • Could access to spell “Marionette”. • Could access to reform “Marionette Ascension”. • Costs 2 picks. Archmage: The wizard is a renowned master in teaching and training spell casting. • Increases both already acquired and newly produced skill points (SP) by 50%. • Could access to reform “Archmage’s Tutition”. • Could access to reform “Archmage’s Mentorship”. Artificer: The wizard is a master craftsman who is an expert in magical engineering. • Reduces the cost of making items/artifacts by 50%. • Starts the game with the "Enchant Item" spell already researched. • The "Create Artifact" spell will be the first researchable Rare level spell. • All mechanical units trained by the wizard gain +1 Melee/Range Attack, +1 Armor, +1 Resistance, +1 Movement Point, and magic weapons. • Could access to spell “Clockwork Tinmen”. • Could access to spell “Clockwork Factory”. • Could access to spell “Rebuild”.
PDF page 5 Conjurer: The wizard is an expert in conjuring magical creatures. • Reduces the casting costs of all summoning spells by 25%. • Reduces the research costs of all summoning spells by 25%. • Reduces the total upkeep cost of Fantastic creatures by 25%. • Starts the game with the "Summoning Circle" spell already researched. • Could access to spell “Conjuring Pact”. • Could access to spell “Spirit Link”. Sage Master: The wizard is a renowned scholar. • Increases total research points generated each turn by 33%. • Increases research points by 15 RP each turn. • Library, University, Sage's Guild, Academy, and Ludus Agoge cost 15% cheaper. • Could access to reform “Education Reform”. • Could access to spell “Arcane Conference”. Myrran: The wizard is native to the plane of Myrror. • Starts the game with a fortress on the plane of Myrror. • Allows the player to choose Myrran races as their home race. • Adjusts the starting positions of AI wizards accordingly. • Could access to spell “Astral Gate”. Guardian : The wizard is respected as the guardian protector of his people. • Increases the maximum population of the home race's city by 6 units. • In combat, all units controlled by the wizard gain +10% To-Hit, +10% To-Defend, and +1 Resistance when defending the city controlled by the wizard. • Could access to reform “Lord Liberator”. • Could access to reform “Lord Protector”. • Costs 2 picks. Famous Benefactor: The wizard is well-known as a benefactor who willingly lends a hand to those who serve under them. • Starts the game with 30 fame, and the "Heroic Heart" spell already researched. • All heroes controlled by the wizard gain +2 Melee/Range Attack, +1 Armor, and +1 Resistance. • 2x chance for artifact merchants, and 4x chance for mercenaries offer. • If have enough gold, a hero is guaranteed to appear for hire in January, an item merchant appears in July and mercenaries always show up in April and October starting in 1502. • Heroes and mercenaries offering to join will be at a 1 level higher than usual and hiring cost of them do not increase by their level. • Could access to spell “Bountiful Festivity”. Runemaster: The wizard has mastered the power of rune language. • Reduces research costs of Arcane spells by 50%. • Reduces casting costs of overland spells (except Arcane, summons, and enchantments) by 25%. • Reduces casting costs of overland Arcane spells (except item creation, and summons) by 50%. • Reduces casting costs of combat Arcane spells by 25%. • The effects of dispel-type spells cast by the wizard are 100% more effective. • Starts the game with the "Dispel Magic" spell already researched. • Could access to spell “Rune Formation Array”.
PDF page 6 Charismatic: The wizard possesses an unnatural presence that dramatically improves his dealings with others. • Reduces the costs for hiring heroes, mercenaries, and purchasing magical items by half. • Reduces the unrest level in all cities owned by the wizard by 1. • Halves all diplomatic penalties from negative actions. • Doubles all positive diplomatic effects. • Offers made by the wizard are significantly more likely to be accepted. • Could access to spell “Rally”. • Could access to spell “Denoucement”. • Could access to spell “Persuasive Whisperer”. Specialist: The wizard invests their skill and effort into mastering their primary realm. Primary realm is determined by the realm with the highest number of books. In case of a tie, specialist realms are prioritized in this order: Nature, Sorcery, Chaos, Life, and Death. • Reduces the casting costs for spells in the wizard's primary realm by 12%. • Reduces the research costs for spells in the wizard's primary realm by 12%. • Increases dispel resistance for spells in the wizard's primary realm by 50%. • Could access to reform “Gaia Mastery”. • Could access to reform “AEther Mastery”. • Could access to reform “Chaos Mastery”. • Could access to reform “Life Mastery”. • Could access to reform “Death Mastery”. Tactician: The wizard is renowned for their skill in maneuvering troops in combat. • The wizard can sneak attack, making defenders lose their first action unless it's another wizard's fortress, they have Tactician, or Supernatural Primal power protects them. • All the wizard's units gain +1 Armor. • The wizard's teleporting units gain First Strike. • The wizard's Non-Corporeal units gain Negate First Strike. • The wizard's units with a terrain bonus gain double the bonus, First Strike, and Negate First Strike. • Gets a bonus in strategic combat. • Could access to spell “Tactical Drill”. • Could access to spell “Tactical Recall”. • Could access to spell “Strategic Recall”. • Costs 2 picks. • Mutually exclusive with the Warlord retort at the start of the game. Omniscient Procurator : The wizard is an expert in managerial and statecraft. • Reduces "Indirect Control" and "Banished" city penalties by 25%. • Triples the "Administrative Skill" bonus. • Could access to spell “Town Portal”. Cult Leader: The Wizard is the leader of a religion/cult with strong influence over the believers. Religious buildings include the Shrine, Monastery, Witches' Convent, Cathedral, and Temple. Certain buildings and city enchantments may be sanctified into religious buildings through certain spells. • Increases the power generated by religious buildings by 100%. • Increases the unrest reduction by religious buildings by 50% (rounded down). • Could access to spell “Gospel of Evangelism”. • Could access to spell “Divine Judgement”.
PDF page 7 Astrologer: The wizard is an expert in predicting and manipulating destiny by reading stars. • Nodes controlled by the wizard produce +2 power for each year passed since the start of the game. • Immune to spell-countering effects from nodes. • Could access to spell “Dishearten Prophesy”. • Could access to spell “Lucky Star”. • Costs 2 picks. Spellweaver Enchanter : The wizard is an expert in the art of enchantment. • Reduces the cost of enchantment/curse spells cast by the wizard by 25%. • Increases dispel resistance of all enchantments/curses cast by the wizard by 150%. • Could access to reform “Tatto Magic”. • Could access to spell “Domain of Enchanter”. • Costs 2 picks.
PDF page 8 Difficulties Game difficulty settings in Warlord mod have been adjusted relative to Caster of Magic, with the following key points: • AI upkeep multiplier is for the most part removed. AI doesn't need upkeep immunity to stay challenging. This reduces unit spam considerably. • AI overland spell casting cost multiplier is toned down. • Easiest 2 difficulties do not penalize AI resources. Instead, player is rewarded with power and production bonuses • Hardest difficulties do not reward AI resources as much. Instead, player is handicapped with various city economy penalties. • The 'stalling' AI tactic is introduced in 'advanced' difficulty, tailored towards challenge-seeking players AI Starting Mana Beginner Easy Normal Fair Advanced Expert Master Lunatic Phantasm Score Multiplier 100% 100% 100% 130% 160% 200% 250% 300% 400% Outpost growth 90% 90% 90% 100% 110% 120% 120% 120% 130% Fortress Lightning Strength 0% 50% 50% 100% 100% 150% 150% 150% 150% AI City Growth 100% 100% 100% 100% 110% 120% 120% 120% 130% AI Overland spell casting cost 95% 95% 95% 90% 80% 70% 70% 70% 60% AI Production multiplier 85% 85% 85% 100% 115% 130% 130% 130% 145% AI Gold multiplier 100% 100% 100% 115% 130% 150% 150% 150% 175% AI Power multiplier 100% 100% 100% 110% 125% 150% 150% 150% 180% AI Research multiplier 90% 90% 90% 110% 125% 150% 150% 150% 170% AI Upkeep multiplier 100% 100% 100% 100% 100% 100% 100% 100% 80% AI Hero Experience multiplier 0% 0% 50% 100% 150% 200% 250% 300% 350% Fortress Lightning Duration multiplier 0% 50% 100% 100% 100% 150% 150% 150% 150% AI Starting Gold 75 75 120 140 200 350 350 350 500 0 0 30 35 60 125 125 125 200 Monster spawn multiplier (from original) 50% 100% 100% 100% 100% 105% 105% 105% 120% Highest allowed monster (from original) 50% 100% 100% 110% 120% 130% 130% 130% 150% AI Wizard picks 12 12 12 12 12 12 12 13 14 Human Capital Power Bonus 50 25 Human City Production Fixed Bonus 10 5 Human Penalty gold,res,food,prod (round down) 10% 20% 25% Human Penalty Unrest 5% 10% 15% 20%
PDF page 9 Building and City Changes: Summary: Early city progression is slowed due to generally higher production costs, reduction in early fixed production bonuses, and less accessible higher-tier production buildings. The changes partially bring back the city progression pace of the original Master of Magic early game through late game. The amount of starting overland skill is approximately 2 to 4 below Caster of Magic to balance city vs magic production early in the game. Economy buildings are more interconnected via pre-requisites (dependencies) and are inspired by a few building tree mechanics choices from the original Master of Magic. Tree of knowledge carries a higher research and casting cost (2000 and 250, respectively) and also unlocks Maritime's Guild, Wizard's Guild and Amplifying Tower. Unlocked economy buildings all share the same building prerequisite: Sage's Guild. Several economy buildings take more time to build, but gold maintenance of economy buildings generally reduced with a city with all buildings typically saving roughly 20 gold per turn. However, there are 2 contributors to gold loss in this mod: non-capital income penalty, and higher unit upkeep costs. What makes you poor is not your own cities simply existing, but having an excessive number of units. This helps make game less cluttered and come with end turn savings. Early military aided by bringing back Master of Magic's Armory as an early recruitment building. It requires more investment to develop a military city that pumps out experienced and magic-weapon units. This was needed to balance the superior, less disposable nature of normal units. Non-Capital cities are less productive , they receive a penalty to gold, food, production, power based on their distance from capital city. Mountain terrain have a 5% production bonus (instead of 7%). Volcanic terrain retain their 7% bonus. Trade income cap per city is now 2% per pop (from 3% per pop). Early Buildings: Mill (cost 80/1) – No longer a massive production boost to new towns. Redesigned to grant 1 prod + ½ production per active farmer, yielding significantly more hammers in large cities (v 1.4.17 adjusted rounding issues). Sawmill is no longer an essential early building to jump start a new town's production. Dock (cost 120/0) – Now grants 1 food per ocean, coast, and rivermouth tile NEW! Shipyard (cost 300/1) – Split from Dock and become requirement for Galley and Fire Galley Smithy (cost 75/0) – Grants 3 fixed production (4+ in good terrain) and most units no longer require it. Alchemist's Guild (cost 150/2) Alchemist Guild now grants +2 research – bringing back the original master of magic feature of it granting a minor economy bonus. Cost is noticeably higher however. Barracks (cost 200/1) – Barracks, which now require armory, delays starting experience boosts similar to Original Master of Magic. This is needed to balance the enhanced stats among starter units and helps keep them viable for a bit longer due to their low recruitment cost, while benefiting later units as well. NEW! Armory (cost 150/1) – Armory has been restored from original Master of Magic, being the building for recruiting the next tier of spearmen units (e.g. halberdiers), a few unique racial units below the level of Fighter's Guild, and a secondary requirement for many support units like magisters. Units from armory typically a midpoint between starter units and fighter's guild units. They tend to be cost effective and melee-oriented.
PDF page 10 Fighter's Guild (cost 200/2) – Recruits the next tier of swordsmen, bowmen, and cavalry units (all unique to Warlord mod) if permitted by race, as well as a few unique racial units. Troops more advanced than what is provided by Armory. War College (cost 540/3), now requires Fighter's Guilds and grants a racial unique unit for two races (Dwarf, Gnoll), both cost effective given they recruit with a minimum of veteran experience level. War College help keep bottom-tier and mid-tier units viable due to their lower recruitment cost while waiting for Tree of Knowledge. Stables (cost 120/2) – Grants 4 fixed production (5 to 6 in good terrain). Miner's Guild (cost 200/2) - Considerably more expensive, worth building once town is reasonably grown. Mechanician's Guild (cost 400/4) – Changed to give +1.5 prod per worker (w/ +1/2 from town hall it adds to +2). Considerably more expensive, worth building once town is reasonably grown. This building increasing opportunity cost when accomodating food upkeep. Also grants 2 mid-tier mechanical units of higher usefulness than Caster of Magic's catapult. Town Hall (cost 80/0) – (previously known as Builder Hall) Allows buildings associated with advanced civilizations, but also grants 0.5 production per worker, which is approximately a 15-20% production boost. Marketplace (80/0). Income reduced to 7 (from 8). Farmer's Market (cost 150/1) – Population growth bonus reduced by 10. Instead of granting food, Farmer's Market grants 0.5 gold per population. NEW! Brewery (cost 200/2) – Consume portion of Foods produce in city based on number of pop unit and convert to gold at rate 4 Gold per Food. Forester's Guild (130/1). Grants 4 food but gives +2 for each wild game resource in vicinity. Magic Market (100/0) – had power income reduced to 4. Library (80/0) – had research income reduced to 4. Monument (75/0). University (180/1). Monastery (aka. Parthenon) (cost 200/1) – Priests no longer recruited here. Cathedral (cost 500/2) Cathedral allows inquisitors (high men) and now grants 2 unrest reduction. NEW! Temple (cost 400/1) – the alternative of Cathedral for some races, allows priests. The alternative Temple building only grants 4 power and 1 unrest, but can be built faster and grants 3 power and 1 unrest for each nightshade, orihalcon ,and wild game tile in the vicinity of town. NEW! Witches’ Convent (cost 400/3) – Generates 4 religious power and curses enemy units when the city is attacked. NEW! Fortification (cost 600/5) – Requires mechanician guild and wall – All units inside city walls gain 'large shield' effect and city in combat is surrounded by ocean tiles, thus impassable unless water walking, non- corporeal, or flying. If playing with automatic combat, it grants +4 defense to units. NEW! Hillfort (cost 300/3) – Only available for a few races, surround city with impassable cliff face with some choke point to move through. Units inside city area also get Missile Immunity. NEW! Warlord’s Hold (cost 400/5) – Only available for raider races, double strength of unrest reduction through garrison and reduces cost of unit recruitment by 25%.
PDF page 11 Oracle (cost 360/2) Advanced Buildings: Sage's Guild (400/2). Requires University. Grants access to most advanced economy buildings: Linking Towers, Amplifying Tower, Wizard's Guild. All 3 are now linked to 'Tree of Knowledge' Amplifying Tower (900/7) Wizard's Guild (800/3) Linking Towers (500/4) all require Sage's Guild and Tree of Knowledge and intended to be part of late game. You will no longer see high caster units dominating the early game. • Note: Wizard's Guild now grants 12 power and 2 research. Maritime Guild (cost 450/3) and requires Tree of Knowledge. However, warships are far superior in this mod. Armorer's Guild (cost 600/4) and Fantastic Stables (cost 750/4) with a significantly less accessible 'Tree of Knowledge' delays their usage by a couple of years relative to unmodded Caster of Magic. NEW! Hangar (cost 400/3) is a requirement for flying mechanical units. The units recruited from these buildings typically cost 240-300, require 2 Food, and are far more advanced than their Caster of Magic counterparts. These units are not part of the Caster of Magic design of being disposable and inferior to summons and spammed all over the world to the point of clutter. These units, many of which benefit immensely from buffs, can compete against uncommon and rare tier summons and in groups assisted by spells be capable of defeating top tier summons. Building Tree: Ships: Sawmill → (Shipyard + Fighter's) → Maritime Wood Production: Sawmill → Forester's Guild Production: (Miner's Guild + University) → (Mechanician's Guild + Wall) → Fortification Food: (Granary + marketplace) → Farmer's Market (Granary + Forester's) → Animist Guild Research: Library + Builder's Hall → (University + Alchemist Guild) → Sage's Guild Magic: Marketplace → Magic Market + Sage's Guild → Wizard's Guild Combat Skill: ( Monument + Sage's Guild) → Linking Tower Overland skill: Sage's Guild → Amplifying Tower Gold: (Marketplace + University) → (Bank + shipyard) → Merchant's Guild Military: Armory → Fighter's Guild → Coliseum/War College/Armorer's Guild/Fantastic Stables Armory → Barracks → War College (with Fighter's Guild) Fighter's Guild + Barracks grant Colosseum, also grants War College (with Fighter's Guild) Religion: (Shrine + Town Hall)→ Oracle and Monastery. Monastery → Cathedral/Temple (Shrine + Magic Market) → Witches’ Convent. Note that Tree of Knowledge unlocks Amplifying Tower, Linking towers, Wizard's Guild, Armorer's Guild, Fantastic Stable, and Maritime Guild

Construction 1 Spearmen used mainly for unrest reduction at a minimum cost, but the high figure count allows buff strategies against non-ranged units and cheap early game stacks. The original spearmen's role was too limited to be of use, filling a mostly useless slot (given that swordsmen are more durable for sacrificial units when engaging in wars of attrition via spells). Delayed access to barracks keep these from getting too useful. Swordsmen (smithy), Bowmen (sawill + smithy), and Cavalry (stables + smithy) are the stock low-tier units. Swordsmen have decent melee, high armor vs ranged and spells, and perform well if aided by experience boosters and unit enchantments. Bowmen are your traditional ranged units, the extra 5% to hit helps them be more accurate at mid-range. Cavalry (unchanged from caster of magic) are your fast, tactical unit, but highly vulnerable to multi-figure attacks. Delayed access to barracks keep these enhanced bottom-tier units balanced. Halberdiers (armory) are superior to swordsmen, particularly when facing other melee units. They are designed to be more like their Master of Magic armory units in terms of cost and effectiveness, thus they lose 1 resistance, 1 racial special attack, and 10 cost. Crossbowmen (fighter's guild + library) are the next bowmen tier, have fewer figures, but attack with armor piercing shots and protect themselves with large shield. They are however vulnerable to melee.
PDF page 13 Shieldbearers (fighter's guild) are the next swordsmen tier. These have mediocre melee damage output for the cost (same as halberdier), but come with higher movement and very high armor, particularly against ranged and magical attacks thanks to their large shield perk. Heavy Cavalry (fighter's guild + stables) are the next cavalry tier, with higher stats across the board but 1 less movement. First strike can be highly effective with 7 base attack, and the armor deficiency of Cavalry is lessened with 4 base armor rating, making this a well-rounded tactical unit. Shamans (shrine) and Monks (monastery) only differ by their movement rating. Priests (cathedral) now carry 2 healing charges and 1 resist to all making them a very impactful support unit, but have poor damage potential, high upkeep cost, and require Temple, a pretty advanced building. These units do not count as trespassers when you have a wizard's pact. Disciples (sage's guild) are low-tier mages. Magisters (wizard's guild + armory) are mages that have large shield instead of missile immunity, to simulate magic resistance. Along with 2 extra shots, this is generally an improvement, thus are balanced out by having 1 fewer movement point. Mechanician's Guild is much harder to build, thus stock units from it are superior. Catapults are now more damaging, durable, and carry more ammo. Ballista is an alternative mechanical unit that loses wall crushing, vulnerable to missile immunity in favor of armor piercing shots. These units give economy-oriented races viable defenses Triremes (dock) and Galleys (shipyard + armory) are unchanged but gold upkeeps are returning to ships Fire Galley (shipyard + mechanician guild) are a more melee-oriented, faster ship that can attack flyers. Warships come with higher stats and a much higher cost and upkeep with fewer races being able to build these and tree of knowledge now needed to unlock Maritime's Guild. Engineers (university + town hall) can now move, cast 'sapping wall' and buff mechanical units by +20% To-Hit and +10% To-Defend, giving them tactical use in battle. Their cost and building requirements have been increased due to them building roads 50% faster than unmodded engineers. Pioneers (town hall + fighter's guild) are inferior engineers for some races that do not specialize on road building, build 33% as fast as a modded engineer (and 50% as fast as unmodded engineers). These may be subject to change as effect on elves and halflings are being reviewed. Armorer Guild and Fantastic Stable unit – typically cost 240-300 5-6 gold upkeep 2 food upkeep. These top-tier units are not part of the Caster of Magic design of being disposable and inferior to summons. These units, many of which benefit immensely from buffs, can compete against uncommon and rare tier summons and in groups assisted by spells be capable of defeating top tier summons.

PDF page 15 Race Summary / Units: Intro: Brief race descriptions and general strategies have been included in the manual to ease the player into trying out each race. Unit stats were kept hidden in the manual for conciseness and also to preserve the excitement of discovery when noticing new units. Note that some normal units will come with spell charges , some of which cannot be countered. Barbarian: Military-Oriented Gameplay Characteristics: 90 growth, +30 outpost growth, Cheap settlers, Special Building: Altar of Storm (required shore) Building Limitations: Alchemist's Guild, (+Sage's Guild, +Wizard's Guild, +Amplifying Tower, +Linking Towers), Monastery, (+Cathedral/Temple), Bank, (+Merchant's Guild), Armorer's Guild, Fantastic Stables, Mechanician's Guild (+Fortification, +Hanger) Barbarian design is to overwhelm opponents early on with mobile overland units (pathfinding) that deal very high-damage due to having an innate +10% to hit and extra thrown secondary attacks. The high outpost and city growth and cheap settlers ensure you have numerous sufficiently developed military centers producing strong mid-tier units (Barbarians lack a top tier unit). If military superiority on land is not enough, barbarians also rule the seas via a unique naval ship. Note: barbarians no longer have a resistance penalty. They have access to the majority of unrest-reduction and production buildings to ensure population remains loyal and productive to your cause. However, Barbarians have severe limitations to strictly gold and power sources, thus players must engage in conquest to stay competitive. The current design addresses some of the issues that made race inferior in Master of Magic. However, a different balancing method was applied to restore the race's themes and challenges the notion that a race must have access to several advanced buildings, even wizard's guild, to stay competitive. Normal Units: +10% To-Hit, Pathfinder, +Thrown (up to 4 per figure) Spearmen, Swordsmen, Bowmen, Cavalry, Shamans, Heavy Cavalry. PDF page 16 Special Units: Berserkers (Fighter's Guild, Cost 90) More durable than in Caster of Magic. These continue being high damage dealers and vulnerable to curses and ranged attacks. Spellserkers (Fighter's Guild and Animist Guild, Cost 120): Now requiring only Fighter's Guild and Animist Guild, these sturdy melee mage units are also the most easily accessible Caster 20 unit in the game. Gladiators (Coliseum, Cost 175): These are the most durable units Barbarians can offer. They operate in a similar fashion to stock unit shieldbearer with more advanced stats and hp. Longship (fighter's guild + ship yard, Cost 140): Far superior to galley with reasonable building requisites and cost. The only ship that comes with more than 1 figure and specializes in speed and melee (ranged attacks are present with only 4 ammo) . If Mariner Mastery is present, this ship can reach enemies in 1 turn. If enchanted with flying, Longship turns into a general purpose upper-tier unit.
PDF page 17 Gnoll: Military-Oriented Gameplay Characteristics: 60 growth, avg outpost growth, +2 attack, +1 move Special Building: Altar of the Moon (required swamp) Building Limitations: Monastery (+Cathedral/Temple), Maritime Guild, Armorer's Guild, Fantastic Stables, University, +Bank, +Merchant's Guild, +Sage's Guild), Mechanician's Guild, (+Hanger, +Fortification), (+Wizard's Guild, +Amplifying Tower, +Linking Towers) Gnoll is designed to be an early rush aggressive race, even more so than Barbarians. This means terrible economic potential on their own, but outstanding and mobile military units ideal for early war. A unique theme of Gnolls is how some units appear to be a tier above what the unlocking building would otherwise provide. Players starting with Gnolls cannot excel without early conquest. Unlike Barbarians, Gnolls cannot build beyond the starter buildings and have merely average growth potential (towns, outposts, settler production). Their armies, if unsuccessful at conquest early, will not be able to keep up against more advanced, productive civilizations. Units are also unable to hit flying units effectively. Because of these limitations, it did not seem fair to punish Gnolls with a poor armorer's guild unit, thus Jackal Riders improved and moved to require War College instead (which can be rushed without Tree of Knowledge). Additionally, as an early rush race, the magic market limitation was too harsh, thus had to be reevaluated. The race is balanced by adding advanced building limitations instead. PDF page 18 Special Units: Hunters (Replaces Bowmen, cost 40): Initially underwhelming, but with 3 modes of attack (melee, thrown, range), ability to install trap, and a small 5% to hit bonus, it becomes formidable with experience, special magic weapons, and attack buffs like 'fiery fury’ Wolf Riders (Stables, cost 70): Stables granting you access to a tier-2 like unit. Besides 5 move, it comes with pathfinder to hunt for easy victims and be assisted by other mobile units and summons (e.g. hell hounds). 80 cost was evaluated as being too high for a rush race, thus reduced to 70. Witch Doctors (shrine, magic market, cost 90): Shaman with mid-tier unit properties, such as high ranged poison damage, double hp, and 2 charges of weakness spell. This is a viable unit for players who prefer to develop the town economically first (see building requisites) and this unit's fullest potential is early in the game when 'weakness' and poison work best. Marauder (fighter's guild, cost 120): Updated beyond a first-strike shieldbearer with extraordinary stats. With high base damage, they can defeat a unit without taking damage. Outside of melee, they are hard to defeat with 18 base hp and large shield, making them effective garrison units. Jackal Riders (war college, cost 190): Mobile melee unit with 'cause fear' and top-tier qualities without the need of Tree of Knowledge and thanks to being unlocked by War College, comes with additional stats. It does come with several vulnerabilities due to its high figure count and low armor (e.g. immolation) as well as mediocre resistance. Nevertheless, this is an outstanding unit for the low cost.
PDF page 19 Halflings: Economy-oriented Gameplay Characteristics: 60 growth, +40 outpost growth, +1 research per pop, +2 food per pop, low unrest of conquered towns Special Building: Academy (required mountain/hill/volcano) Building Limitations: Barracks (+Colosseum, +War College), Monument, (+Linking Towers), Armorer's Guild, Temple, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Halfling are an economy race that needs spell support to assist in aggression. They can develop outposts into towns faster than any other race, can build most economy buildings, and their population comes with food and research bonuses, encouraging numerous well-developed gold, research and power centers and summon- oriented gameplay. Note that animist guild can be built and modded accordingly to allow halfling farmers to produce 8 food. Race can now even build roads, albeit slowly, with 'pioneer' unit. Their troops are however mediocre to poor due to higher recruitment costs of early units combined with lack of access to barracks and war college, requiring use of 'heroism' to be viable. In fact, a swordsman unit with heroism + holy armor + discipline is borderline overpowered this early in the game, an option available to players. All combat units revolve around 1hp per figure and are primarily ranged, making them highly vulnerable to large shield and especially missile immune units. For the late game, they needed something in terms of units and something not fully dependent on buffs. It was decided a tactical flying unit with fairly low attack power fits the overall theme of the race best. As a balancing factor, a few building restrictions that entirely impact battles (e.g. monument, linking towers) were introduced. Normal Units: Lucky, higher unit cost, -1 Melee Pioneers, Spearmen, Swordsmen, Bowmen, Disciples, Shamans, Magisters Generic Mechanical Units: Lucky, -1 Melee Trireme, Galley, Fire Galley, Warship, Catapult, Ballista race unit cost Figures Melee throw/breath Range Ammo Armor Resist Health to hit Move Poison ToDefend Halfling Spearmen 15 8 1 2 4 1 0.4 2 0.4 Halfling Bowmen 40 6 1 3 8 2 5 1 0.45 2 0.4 Halfling Swordsmen 40 8 3 4 5 1 0.4 2 0.4 Halfling Shamans 75 4 1 3 4 3 7 1 0.4 3 0.4 Halfling Disciples 75 4 1 4 6 3 6 1 0.4 2 0.4 Halfling Slingers 80 8 1 4 6 2 6 1 0.4 3 0.4 Halfling Scouts 90 2 2 6 3 0.4 6 0.4 Halfling Magisters 150 4 1 7 6 3 9 1 0.4 2 0.4 Halfling Rocs 280 2 8 7 9 9 0.4 6 0.4 Special Units: Scouts (stables, cost 90) – clearly not a combat unit, but you have access to a 'stealth' unit for exploration of enemy territory and to keep in nodes near opponent cities. Slingers (armory, cost 80) – improved somewhat with lower cost and higher mobility, and most importantly becoming again a unit that can be recruited with armory. It remains surprisingly poor outside of life wizard 'heroism + discipline' strategies which fulfill unit's full potential to deal significant range damage while being able to withstand a few attacks. Rocs (Fantastic Stables, cost 280) – A flying 6 move first strike unit that can dodge arrows (missile immunity) but suffers from lack of barracks and war college, resulting in mediocre stats unless buffed. Its main strength is having the highest movement speed alongside Doom Bats for exploration, sneak attacks, combat stalling strategies, and picking off ranged units.
PDF page 20 High Elf: Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 30 growth, +20 outpost growth, +1/2 power per pop Special Building: Tree of Life (required forest) Building Limitations: Maritime Guild, Temple, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent High Elves have economic potential due to access to all economy buildings, citizens that provide passive power income, and outposts that develop faster than average They are now capable of building roads, albeit slowly. Their downside is a very low city population growth rate and with smaller population, gold and production is therefore lower as a result. Their generic troops are good due to the racial bonuses. Mid tier stock units with these benefits become formidable troops with heavy cavalry's first strike, combined with to hit bonus can result in killing an opponent before they get the chance to strike back. They also have 3 top tier units with very different roles, for you to shift around your strategies based on your opponents or lair targets. The race design is not much different from Caster of Magic, but Pegasi were reevaluated and made into a proper top-tier unit with high cost and maintenance, not a buff-dependent cavalry + bowmen that flies unit. Normal Units: +10% To-Hit, Forester, +1 Resistance Pioneers, Spearmen, Swordsmen, Disciples, Cavalry, Halberdiers, Shieldbearers, Heavy Cavalry. PDF page 21 Special Units: Longbowmen (forester's guild, cost 50): significantly boosted, matching the relative power of the original Master of Magic unit by having higher ranged, to hit, and even long range. Druids (wizard's guild, cost 150): Magicians with priest-like properties that can also cast 'resist elements'. Their racial bonus helps them deal high damage. Rangers (armorer's guild, cost 200) : The most damaging bow-and-arrow unit in Arcanus, moved from Nomads and given High Elf's excellent racial bonuses. The unit also has pathfinder, helpful to increase mobility of Elven Lords, and stealth. The problem with this unit is how 'animate ammo', 'wall of darkness' or other counters can render it useless. Elven Lords (armorer's guild, cost 250): Damage and durability boosts, but with a significant cost increase. This unit specializes in sheer melee force with first strike armor piercing and is a great candidate for buff spells. Pegasus Riders (fantastic stables, cost 280): Higher stats across the board, particularly in regards to melee, but at more than double the cost. This is a tactical unit that works best when Pegasus Riders can use all available ammo. Pegasus Riders are however vulnerable to missile counters like 'animate ammo' and their melee capabilities are comparable to a mid-tier unit.
PDF page 22 High Men: Tilted Towards Economy Gameplay Characteristics: 60 growth, +10 outpost growth, Buildings cost 20% less, +1 rebel, Special Building: Sancta Basilica (required desert) Building Limitations: Fantastic Stable, Temple, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent High men have average to strong economic potential due to access to all economy buildings and citizens that can construct buildings at a 20% lower cost (including military buildings). Their downside is having an unrest citizen for every city in addition to unrest modifiers. This race had some controversial design choices. For starters, a -2 resistance penalty is far too severe to be fun. The crusader unit in Caster of Magic was absurdly overpowered in the hands of a smart player to the point of causing tedium. By reducing the resistance penalty, adjusting mid-tier units, and adding a more pure-might but lower cost top unit, the race feels more three dimensional, varied, and ultimately fun. The race still specializes quite well against defeating lairs and nodes with powerful high-figure units. The +2 figures theme has also been expanded to more units, mainly support-type units. Normal Units: +2 Figures to some stock units, -1 Resistance Spearmen, Swordsmen, Bowmen, Engineer, Cavalry, Monks, Crossbowmen, Disciples, Magisters Their troops start out weak with no bonuses other than a resistance penalty. However, the later stock units come with +2 figures, increasing durability and damage output. High Men also offer a great variety of units, thus can adapt to different battle needs. PDF page 23 Special Units: Pikemen (Armory, 60 cost). These come at a lower cost in this mod, but with weaker defensive stats. These carry the design of spearmen-like units being fragile (especially against ranged) but dealing high damage, in this case 8 armor piercing hits at a base swordsmen attack level. Their high 8-figure count makes it an excellent target for buff spells. Squires (Fighter's Guild, 80 cost). Replacing Caster of Magic's overpowered 60 cost “Crusaders” with a more damaging unit, with more armor but less resistance, and without healing spell at 80 cost. These still have large shield, making them robust units against ranged attacks. Their high 8-figure count makes it an excellent target for buff spells. Knights (Fighter's Guild + Stable, 120 cost). Now follows the 'heavy cavalry template', but with boosts to mobility, damage, and durability (large shield) benefits to being a racial unique. This is a very solid unit for general use. Inquisitors (Cathedral, 120 cost). Priest-like unit with a weak version of exorcise ability for melee and ranged attacks, allowing it to banish lower resistance fantastic units if they fail a resistance check. This ability has a stronger effect against raise undead units. Crusaders (Armorer's Guild + Monastery, 170 cost). Crusaders have been redesigned as a top tier unit and with different visuals. These are now 6 figure large shield troops with higher movement (3), good upper-tier melee and durability stats, and can cast 'holy armor' on self or others. Paladins (Armorer's Guild + Cathedral, 270 cost). Top Tier support unit (Holy Bonus) with decent but unspectacular melee capabilities. Paladins can now cast bless spell (twice) and come with much higher resistance, making them nearly immune to all curse-like attacks and spells and restoring some of the enjoyment from the original where the paladin just couldn't be cursed. They also are immune to illusions.
PDF page 24 Klackons: Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 110 growth, +20 outpost growth, +1 hammer per citizen, -4 rebels (if starter race), + rebels (if not), bad race relations Special Building: Undercity Hive Network Building Limitations: Fantastic Stable, Coliseum, Monastery, (+Cathedral/temple), Merchant's Guild, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Klackons enjoy the fastest city growth in the game. When combined with extra worker productivity and far lower unrest (if starter race), they are able to surpass other races in getting cities fully developed, and earn excessive amount of gold via taxes. Playing with retort 'alchemist' and converting gold to mana is a very powerful strategy. The high production also can lead to producing a large number of military units, helpful when units (especially later) are unimpressive on a power to cost ratio. Your military is defined as 'quantity over quality' and with quantity comes accumulating upkeep costs. It is preferable to rush settlers and cover as much land as possible with klackon cities to enjoy their low unrest, and thus build your economy. You may raze enemy cities to allow room for additional klackon cities overrunning each continent. One problem with this concept in Caster of Magic is the sheer lack of unit diversity: pretty much just halberdiers and stag beetles and they are rather boring units themselves. When the obvious strategy is to maximize the number of klackon cities, it gets repetitive. There is more diversity in this mod, covering one of the main weaknesses of the race in Caster of Magic and making it far more satisfying to play. PDF page 25 Special Units: Stingers (Armory, Cost 70): a halberdier unit with an added poison 1 attack per figure (6 poison). Mantis (Fighter's Guild, Cost 100): 6-figure military troops that also has first strike and higher mobility. However, with 5 base melee, the first strike is not overly impactful, but is yet another element that adds to the high durability (e.g. 7 base armor) of this unit. The seemingly mediocre unit has been proven to win the game on lower difficulties with warlord retort and unit buff strategies. Antlion (Stables, Animist Guild, cost 120): A teleporting heavy cavalry type unit (lacking first strike) with lower melee but 'merging' (teleporting) ability. This ability is restrained by a very low 2 movement, making it impossible to use hit and run tactics . This is among the less cost-effective mid-tier units in the game, but a player has opportunities to exploit the rare 'merging' ability (the only teleporting normal unit) with mobility spells, allowing hit & run tactics. Stag Beetle (Stables, Armorer's Guild, cost 240). As Caster of Magic described it, a true avatar of mediocrity. It has been enhanced in this mod but with a 50% cost increase and a much more significant upkeep increase (the upkeep cost of 1 in Caster of Magic was baffling and made race snowball in gold income). Base armor was reduced to 6 but base to defend increased to 40%, thus has the potential to be very hardy with adamantium, experience and holy bonus. With Klackon's high production output, it is easy to generate a full stack of 8+ fairly easily and cover replacements as needed. This is also Klackon's answer to flying units, being able to hit flyers. Maiden Queen (Wizard's Guild, Animist Guild, cost 240). Later in the game, the mantis units (or Stag Beetle's resistance) need a boost. This is a special support unit that grants +1 to all stats, heals, and also has caster skill 20. It is also relatively hard to kill, engages in melee, and even flies. Wizard's Guild is a hard to access building, thus these will not come into play until the second half of your game.
PDF page 26 Lizardmen: Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 70 growth, +30 outpost growth, NEW +1/4 max pop per tundra, cheaper, faster swimming settlers (note, no longer with fewer rebel bonus) Special Building: Baray (required river) Building Limitations: Fantastic Stables, Ship Yard, (+Maritime Guild, +Merchant's Guild), Miner's Guild (+Mechanician Guild, +Fortification, +Hanger), Cathedral, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Lizardmen excel at early expansionism: marking your territory outside your main continents via fast, swimming settlers. As an incentive to player, settlers are cheaper, more faster, swim, and their outposts grow much faster than average. Early military is oriented towards expansionist playstyles thanks to favorable military logistics and high hp units. Race has limitations to gold and especially production buildings, slowing down construction and unit-recruitment on an individual city basis. However, allowed enough time, Lizardmen cities are rather comprehensive in economic bonuses and late military units excel at city defense. More unit types were added, including a cavalry unit and a mage-like unit., and the design of an Armorer's Guild unit costing only 100 (And acting like one) was challenged. Normal Units: +1 Health, -1 Resistance, Swimming Spearmen, Swordsmen, Bowmen, Shaman, Shieldbearer, Priests Generic Mechanical Units: +1 Health, -1 Resistance Trireme race unit cost Figures Melee throw/breath Range Ammo Armor Resist Health to hit Move Poison ToDefend Lizardman Spearmen 15 8 2 2 2 2 0.3 2 0.3 Lizardman Bowmen 30 6 1 3 8 2 3 2 0.35 2 0.3 Lizardman Swordsmen 30 6 4 4 3 2 0.3 2 0.3 Lizardman Reptile Riders 45 4 5 3 4 4 0.3 4 0.3 Lizardman Shamans 60 4 2 3 4 3 6 2 0.3 3 0.3 Lizardman Marines 65 6 5 4 4 3 0.3 2 0.3 Lizardman Shieldbearers 90 6 5 5 5 3 0.3 3 0.3 Lizardman Javelineers 100 6 5 4 4 6 3 5 2 0.3 3 0.3 Lizardman Priests 120 4 3 4 4 4 7 3 0.3 2 0.3 Lizardman Sea Hags 120 3 5 4 6 4 0.3 3 2 0.3 Lizardman Dragon Turtle 240 1 13 8 9 12 24 0.3 3 0.4
PDF page 27 Special Units: Carrack (forester’s guild and requires coast, cost 80) – Lizardmen's boat, helps with logistics. Reptile Riders (stable + armory, cost 45) – a cavalry unit with lizardmen's hp racial bonus, and sacrificing a bit of speed for armor. They are the only lizardman unit that cannot swim. Mariners (armory, cost 65) – halberdiers with first strike. However, when fighting in the ocean, mariners gain extra mobility and fire immunity (from submerging) Javalineers (fighter's guild, cost 100) – now comes with higher movement and thrown ability. The race's buff - friendly unit in terms of damage output, but fairly fragile for the cost and mediocre if no buffs are applied to unit. Sea Hags (wizard's guild and requires coast, cost 120) – a mage-like unit with low caster points but 1 spell charge of confusion. Their attacks is poison-based melee, a downgrade from a magister's ranged magic attacks but appropriate for a race that does not specialize in magic. Dragon Turtle (Armorer's Guild + stables, cost 240) was allowed to be a top-tier unit with proper movement, cost and maintenance while keeping the feeling of being a tanky unit. Keep in mind Tree of Knowledge which unlocks Armorer's Guild comes a bit later, thus unit needs to be able to do something besides taking hits and stalling for time. With 40% to defend and the right tools, your dragon turtle can become a borderline unkillable unit with some potential of reaching targets and damaging them.
PDF page 28 Nomad: Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 70 growth, cheap settlers, road-like gold bonuses (without roads), NEW population cap trading bonus removed , NEW +1/2 max pop per desert, NEW +1 Food per desert/tundra tile and +2 food per grassland tile. Special Building: Caravanserai (required desert) Building Limitations: Granary, (+Farmer's Market, Animist's Guild), Fortification, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Nomads suffer heavily from lack of food buildings, requiring a larger number of farmers to maintain army, growing slower than 70 base growth implies (which is 10 less than in Caster of Magic), and reaching population caps, an incentive for players to pick low-production territories or even disregard some locations altogether. One added benefit to race is removal of a population cap trading bonus, which synergizes well with the original road- independent trade bonus. Your typical nomad town will have 50% gold bonus as a minimum which is a significant boost to your economy. While Nomads do not need roads for economy, their race can now hire road- builder units, though these build very slowly. Nomad units are highly resistant to curses and poison, and their typical combination of melee, thrown, and arrows make them great targets for damage-oriented buffs and the effects of experience points. Chaos goes well with this strategy with spells like fiery fury or blazing march, and if combined with life spells, units become near- unstoppable when not facing missile immunities. PDF page 29 Special Units: Horsebowmen (stables + sawmill, cost 50) – redesigned to be essentially what it says it is: bowmen on a horse, not a melee unit with bows, thus melee reduced in favor of more ammo Kardakes (armory, cost 80) – their pikemen were given 4 bow attacks (please note armor piercing carries to all attack types). This is among the most advanced units coming out of armory and kept as is by design as a special racial unit. Dervishes (stable + monastery, cost 100) – mounted monks unit that serves role as explorer unit and mobile clergy support for nomad. This unit trade magic ranged attack for high mobility of light cavalry with pathfinding, and arrow physical ranged attack. Sipahis (stables + fighter's guild, cost 120) – With all 3 damage types and enjoying dependable traits like high resistance, mobility and durability, this strong racial unique is a good target for buffs. Cataphracts (stables + armorer's guild, cost 250) – across-the board improvement over sipahis and similar in design as a mobile, durable unit with 3 attack types. A very good target for buffs, which tend to be a better investment on high-cost units. Griffin Riders (fantastic stables, cost 260) – similar in design (flying first strike unit), just with more armor, hp, and to-hit at a higher cost. Its weakness is the average resistance score – an anomaly for the race – but having an option for a flying melee unit for this race should come with a drawback.
PDF page 30 Orcs: Economy-oriented gameplay Characteristics: 90 growth, -10 outpost growth Special Building: Ludus Agoge (required desert) Building Limitations: Cathedral, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent The Caster of Magic design of Orcs remains in place. This is an economy-oriented race with cities growing rapidly and access to all buildings, ultimately making orc population extremely productive while paying high taxes. Additionally, all Orc units have lowered maintenance costs, so if you produce large armies for defense, for lowering unrest, and for offense, you will save a significant amount of gold per turn. One could argue Orcs is the top (or at least top 3) races in regards to gold income. Given that gold is expected to be plentiful, picking 'alchemist' retort can convert that into significant mana income and as an added bonus help your generic early troops cause more damage in battle with magic weapons. This is a solid beginner race, allowing access to most stock units without any racial modifiers, a couple of top-tier units that are fairly easy to use, and practice with the empire building elements of the game. Normal Units: lower gold upkeep spearmen, swordsmen, bowmen, engineer, cavalry, disciples, shamans, shieldbearers, crossbowmen, heavy cavalry. One weakness is the low resistance but given the unspectacular nature of orc military units, hoplites look pretty good by comparison. Legionaries (Armorer's Guild + Barracks, cost 240) – Caster of Magic horde was incompatible with Orc's advanced technology and were redesigned to follow the roman theme started with hoplites, and now made into a proper armorer's guild unit with high damage and defensive stats. Its signature characteristic is a rare 9-figure count, therefore an excellent target for unit buff spells. The unit also has a few support abilities such as 'healer'. It is a requirement to at least have veteran level experience and/or mithril weapons to make these competitive against other top-tier units. Wyvern Riders (fantastic stables, cost 280) – Wyverns come at near doubled the cost, but are given a total of 28hp, rare for a flying mobile unit, +20% to hit to increase potential of damage outside of poison, and very high poison damage (14 with both figures). For best poison results, pick off low resistance units with this mobile flyer or find ways to lower their resistance.
PDF page 31 Beastmen: Tilted towards economy gameplay Characteristics: 70 growth, -5 outpost growth, +1/2 power per citizen Special Building: Idol of Heavenly Bull (required desert) Building Limitations: Maritime Guild, Cathedral, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Beastmen are the most traditional of the Myrran races. On the economy side of things, you can build nearly everything and even have some passive power income through their population. On the military side, you have a wide variety of stock and racial unique units covering various needs. First strike and other slight boosts were added in the mod to balance the cost increase. Chironean Guards (armorer's guild, stables, cost 260) – Essentially centaurs with far more impressive stats across the board and nearly double the hp, but mediocre resistance. Minotaur (armorer's guild, cost 270) – Reduced to hit but increased to defend (which benefits greatly from 'large shield'). Stats adjusted accordingly but overall boosted to follow the mod's vision of top-tier units. This is your option for extreme melee damage and buff potential to be hardy against ranged attacks. Gugalanna (fantastic stables, cost 290) – Gorgon unit image from Master of Magic is back! This is a flying unit with a -1 modifier stoning gaze (which has its uses against death units or with black prayer) and a high 50% base to hit. Their resistance is higher than the other beastmen top tier units in case you need better protection against curses. Manticores were moved to Rakhshasa.
PDF page 32 Dark Elf Tilted Towards (late) Military Gameplay Characteristics: 30 growth, +20 outpost growth, +1 power per citizen Special Building: Tree of Magic (required forest) Building Limitations: Maritime Guild, Cathedral, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Dark Elves have the original design - being the best race at using magic. This comes in the form of power income bonuses via population and magic-oriented military units having ranged magic attacks, caster skill, magic resistance, or advanced abilities. One downside to this is their fragility relative to other Myrran races and inability to deal high physical damage. However, the top-tier units of Dark Elf, while difficult to obtain and mass-produce, are among the most powerful in the game. Emphasis on caster units gives synergy to 'astrologer' retort, allowing your stacks of caster units to avoid having their spells countered by nodes. The slow population growth dilutes the powerful magic income feature and also negatively impacts gold and production output. However, the race can now hire units to build roads, albeit slowly, boosting gold economy. The most significant changes to this race were additions to mounted mages (magic knight), eliminating the overpowered library-required apprentices, and added emphasis on late-game military domination with abnormally powerful units with high cost and building requisites. PDF page 33 Special Units: Adepts (Sage's Guild, cost 90) – Replaces disciples and acts mainly as a magister with caster 20 that costs less and is more accessible. Magic Knight (Fighter's Guild + Stables, cost 120) – The offensive stats may be mediocre for the cost (5 attack, 5 range w/ 4 ammo, caster 12), not much better than the cost 40 apprentices it replaces and less damaging than an experienced halberdier. It is still considered among the best mid-tier units of the Warlord mod and will likely be a staple unit for dark elf players. Warlocks (Wizard's Guild, cost 180) – largely the same, but now a bit less fragile to magic and ranged attacks (large shield) Nightblades (Armorer's Guild, cost 270) – Unit is able to reliably hurt units unaffected by poison and is surprisingly hardy with the added hp points. They also now have stealth and 3 movement. Nightmares (Wizard's Guild + Fantastic Stables, cost 340) – A heavily redesigned unit, with weaker but illusionary attacks, higher ammo, ability to cast 'terror', and modest boosts in durability. Its jack-of-all-trades nature comes with weaknesses. For starters, all the bells and whistles pushed it to be the most expensive normal unit in the game and also the unit with the most challenging building requisites. Its flying, mobile traits help keep nightmares from trouble, but spells can easily defeat it. The 'terror' spell can only be cast once per combat, diluting the relative power of an army of nightmares. Dark Elf Catapult – loss all range attack and gains 4 charges of Fireball instead.
PDF page 34 Draconians Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 60 growth, -10 outpost growth, flying settlers, +1/2 power per citizen Special Building: Dragon Mound (required mountain/hill/volcano) Building Limitations: Fantastic Stables, Temple, Fortification, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent The flying race in the game, Draconians can scout the map very fast, help settle territory outside your continent, and are great for strategies that rely on combat-cast spells while the enemy can't engage them. They stay close to the Caster of Magic design, with a few adjustments relative to newly introduced units. Their units are excellent due to a combination of added stats, flying abilities, and access to an early 'holy bonus' unit. Ranged units can benefit from being harder to reach with bowmen taking a similar role to Caster of Magic's sprite unit when scouting lairs. Melee units are more convenient with flying with shieldbearers being a great unit to mass-recruit due to lack of noticeable weaknesses. Air Ship (Maritime Guild, cost 200) – Air ship now loses wind-walking ability and not able to perform transporting role but fully dedicated its roles as flying gunship/artillery piece instead. Doom Drakes (Armorer's Guild, cost 280) – Doom drakes have been enhanced with more armor, hp, and +10% to hit and as relatively better units relative to other top-tiers than how they've been in Caster of Magic (they were overpriced and low in damage output).
PDF page 35 Dwarves Economy/Military Mix Gameplay Characteristics: 20 growth, expensive settlers, +50% gold income, 2X resource bonus, +1 production per worker Special Building: Lava Smelter (required mountain/hill/volcano) Building Limitations: Monument +Linking Towers), Stable, (+Fantastic Stable) Magic Market, (+Wizard's Guild) Sage's Guild, (+Wizard's Guild, +Amplifying Tower, +Linking Towers, Hanger) Monument, Merchant's Guild, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent Dwarves are possibly the most overhauled race in Warlord mod. Economically speaking, their building limitations have been shifted around with significant lack of magic-oriented buildings, making 'Alchemist' a retort worth considering when playing race. Their gold and production potential is somewhat improved, if that was even possible. Military-wise, Dwarves have been improved. When consulted with other players, the general consensus was that Dwarf was Myrran's worst race, having severe military deficiencies and gold building limitations that ironically left them with weaker gold income than Beastmen and a few other races. Therefore, Dwarves were given a set of mechanical units and troop-like units, mainly associated with top tier buildings and very high magic resistance. PDF page 36 Special Units: Arquebusiers (alchemist guild + armory, cost 65) – very unique troops, Their mobility and defensive stats are quite poor, relying on cause fear and initial attack acting like first strike, but falling prey to ranged attacks. These also come with weak ranged attacks. This is the kind of complex unit that is mediocre or excellent, based on how you utilize it. Hammerhands (Town hall + fighter's guild, cost 90) – demoted to a mid-tier unit with less melee stats (but flame blade/fiery fury compensates for this weakness). Hammerhands do however move faster and break walls and are far cheaper to produce. They could also work as engineer in building roads too when not as war. Combat Engineer (University + Town Hall, cost 100) – now with triple the road construction speed and redesigned as a support combat unit that has 1 charge of 'flame blade' spell instead of ‘disrupt’ that other engineers have – this spell is excellent on low-damage but sturdy hammerhands. Combat Engineers also have a moderately damaging portable mortar ranged attack and can build roads very quickly. Musketeer (war college + university, cost 160) – carries a similar design to arquebusiers, but with much higher stats. Their mobility and defensive stats (including resistance) are relatively poor and still relying on cause fear and initial attack acting like first strike, but falling prey to ranged attacks. This is a very good target for buff strategies and adamantium minerals and already get recruited with high experience (see building requisite). Steam Cannon (University, cost 120) – Was considered a very disappointing unit, Steam cannon is given more to hit to allow reasonable damage output. They still are nearly immobile and mainly used for defenses. Unit still becomes useless if cast with 'web' Huskarls (Armorer's Guild, cost 250) – Instead of top-tier hammerhands, we have a top tier swordsmen-like unit that deals extreme pain thanks to armor piercing. It is also one of the most durable recruitable units in the game, fitting the theme of dwarves. Golem (Armorer's Guild + Mechanician Guild, cost 275) – It was promoted to a top-tier unit. Golem now has added to hit bonus,higher hp and 40% to defend, and high mobility, acting like a heavy cavalry unit with decent damage output. They come with innate resist elements, which benefits greatly from the added 'to defend' Steam Tank (Armorer's Guild + Mechanician Guild, cost 300) – The ultimate dwarf unit, a ranged mechanical unit that can also deal fire damage in melee (only when attacking). Its various defensive abilities and immunities combined with extreme resistance points limit enemy options that could defeat the unit. However, with only 14hp, these are destructible with the right spells and units.
PDF page 37 Trolls: Military-Oriented Race Characteristics: 60 growth, -20 outpost growth, +1/4 max pop per tundra Special Building: Frost Club Hall (required tundra) Building limitations: Fantastic Stables, Maritime Guild, Monastery, (+Cathedral/Temple), University, +Bank, +Merchant's Guild, +Sage's Guild, (+Wizard's Guild, +Amplifying Tower, +Linking Towers), Mechanician's Guild, (+Hanger) Trolls have been redesigned to be a purely military and very primitive race, so several new building limitations have been established. Additionally, troll units have higher production costs and noticeably higher upkeep costs, severely hurting your economy the larger armies you control. Unlike Barbarians and Gnolls, Troll units remain impressive during the later stages of the game. Their military characteristics are defined by regeneration, high damage, and very high hp ratings and have been enhanced further. PDF page 38 NEW RACE XuanYuan (Myrran) Tilted Towards Economy Race Characteristics: 70 growth, 0 outpost growth. +1 food per farmer. +25% maximum population, cheaper settler Special Building: Military Workshop (required river) Building limitations: Temple/Cathedral, Hanger, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold, Witches’ Convent XuanYuan is a new race introduced by Warlord mod. Eastern Asian inspired with lore about civilization's origins in Arcanus but cursed when seeking immortality and banished into myrror plane. The race gameplay theme is strength in numbers (figures, higher population). Economically, XuanYuan enjoys good population growth and late-game economy thanks to the maximum population bonus and having all buildings accessible to them. The slight increase in food help feed the higher population and larger number of military units. XuanYuan introduces a varied unit roster with different strengths, helping player adapt to challenges. The units come with higher # of figures. The increased figures (+2) benefit the 4-figure units such as crossbowmen and cavalry units the most. A downside is their fragile nature – a 1 armor reduction with no durability bonuses other than their higher figure counts. FireLancer (Armory, cost 65) – 8-figure melee unit with gunpowder, thus 'causing fear' like Dwarf musketeers. Firelancers are strictly melee and excel at it for their low cost. Alchemist (Alchemist Guild + Sage Guild, cost 60) – ranged unit with poison gunpowder, has caster points, and a charge of 'rust'. The unit sacrifices armor piercing in favor of higher base attack. Dragon Guards (Armorer's Guild, cost 190) – A slow and extremely sturdy shieldbearer/swordsmen variant with only 2 figures. Dragon Horses (Fantastic Stable, cost 225) – A flying cavalry (mobile, first strike) unit with well-rounded stats. Dragon Ship (Maritime Guild + Wizard's Guild, cost 300) – A 'ship' that attacks with multiple heads, not unlike a hydra. The dragon ship has melee, breath, and elemental ranged attacks from its 5 heads, resulting in high damage against lower-armored units. It comes with very high hp. Immortals (Linking Towers + Armorer's Guild, cost 320) – An arrogant flying mage hero-like unit with caster 25, a charge of regeneration, several immunities, and good life-draining melee damage output. The immortal cultivator has high hp but is not armored, thus can be easily defeated by repeated low-damage attacks.
PDF page 40 NEW RACE Rakhshasa (Myrran) Tilted Towards Military Race Characteristics: 50 growth, 0 outpost growth, +0.25max pop per forest. +1/2 power per population. Feline race with a gameplay theme of fast bloodsucker carnivore units and multiple units (including a starter unit) with stealth ability. Their military moves fast in the battlefield, their lower-tier generic units are cheap to build, while their more advanced racial uniques all come with the bloodsucker trait (if unit attack deals damage, 3 extra damage is added while unit heals 3 points). This can include separate ranged attacks and thrown attacks, the latter allowing a double-bloodsucker effect. However, a maximum of 1 trigger per attack regardless of # of figures.
