This unit is very vulnerable against resistance-based spells. Jaguar Warriors (Fighter's Guild, cost 110) – This is a shieldbearer with the racial trait bonuses, and bloodsucker trait. A versatile tactical unit. Blood Priests (Temple, cost 120) – The priest gains bloodsucker and racial traits without a unit cost increase. For bloodsucker to work, damage needs to take place and blood priests have very low damage output, so the ability is not as reliable. The ability can also be an opportunity cost to casting the healing spell associated with priests, a guaranteed 5 heal that can apply to any unit. Weretiger Mages (Smithy + Sage Guild, cost 100) – A sturdy caster 14 melee unit with bloodsucker and good durability stats. Bloodsucker may not trigger if its mediocre damage output is blocked by good armor. Unit also has stealth. Rishi (Wizard's Guild + Temple, cost 180) – A sturdy caster 20 + psionic blast charge unit that comes with good durability stats. The damage output (while lower than wizard guild units) is still usually sufficient to trigger the bloodsucker trait. Another benefit of Rishi is illusion immunity, allowing you to see opponent invisible units. Ogre Lord (Armorer's Guild + Coliseum, cost 280) – A powerful, sturdy melee unit with bloodsucker trait. While the unit has impressive attack and armor ratings, the lower hp and resistance make this unit vulnerable in certain situations (against 1-figure units, against spells) Manticore (Fantastic Stable, cost 280) – The unit has been moved from Beastmen, given racial traits such as bloodsucker in place of Beastmen's poison. Instead of ranged attacks, manticore has a weak thrown attack that can help you trigger bloodsucker twice while attacking lower armored units or when thrown attack is buffed with spells or adamantium.
PDF page 42 NEW RACE Goblin (Myrran) Military-Oriented Gameplay Characteristics: 150 growth, 0 outpost growth, -50% tax income through tax avoidance, +3 rebels, bad race relations. Special Building: Mother Fungus (required swamp) Building limitations: Armorer’s Guild, Animist’s Guild, Fantastic Stable, Maritime Guild, Oracle, Wizard’s Guild, Monastery, (+Cathedral/Temple), Merchant’s Guild, Farmer’s Market, Fortification Goblin is a new race introduced by Warlord mod. Goblins are child-sized humanoid fungi, known for their cunning and cruelty. Most races see them as troublesome pests rather than a race to engage with. Goblin cities grow very fast but have very high Unrest, Tax avoidance (-50% tax income). Goblin army emphasis on numerical advantages (consume less food, more figures, melee units could budding clones) but fragile and die quite easily. Goblin lack of late game normal units and most of their late game offensive power coming from mechanical units that both wacky and deadly to itself and others. Normal Units: +2 Figures, -10% To-Defend, -20% Cost, -1 Food Upkeep, melee units could budding clones. Spearmen, Swordsmen, Bowmen Generic Mechanical Units: +2 Figures, -10% To-Defend, -20% Attack strength, -50% Health. Trireme, Galley, Fire Galley, Catapult, Ballista race unit cost Figures Melee throw/breath Range Ammo Armor Resist Health to hit Move Poison ToDefend Goblin Spearmen 12 9 2 2 3 1 0.3 2 0.2 Goblin Swordsmen 24 8 4 4 4 1 0.3 2 0.2 Goblin Bowmen 24 8 1 3 8 2 4 1 0.3 2 0.2 Goblin Hobgoblins 40 8 5 4 4 2 0.35 2 0.2 Goblin Warbosses 120 3 7 5 7 5 0.3 3 0.2 Goblin Spider Riders 80 6 3 4 7 4 0.3 4 3 0.2 Goblin Tricksters 60 4 1 3 7 7 2 0.3 3 1 0.2 Goblin Rabblerousers 65 6 2 3 4 3 6 1 0.3 3 0.2 Goblin Hexers 110 6 2 3 6 3 6 1 0.3 2 1 0.2 Goblin Arsonists 60 8 4 5 3 5 2 0.3 2 0.2 Goblin Night Goblins 90 8 2 5 8 3 5 2 0.35 3 1 0.2 Goblin Mechaniacs 90 6 3 3 6 2 0.3 2 0.2 Goblin Poxbearers 180 4 4 1 6 3 0.3 2 5 0.2 Goblin Doom Wheels 110 3 9 2 7 6 0.3 5 0.2 Goblin Gliders 140 5 2 7 1 7 3 0.3 4 0.2 Goblin Midget Submarines 190 3 5 12 8 5 8 7 0.3 3 0.2 Special Units: Hobgoblins (Armory, Cost 40) – A replacement unit of Halberdiers as 2 nd tier polearm unit, Hobgoblins serve secondary role as road builders as well as main line holder for goblin race with ability to budding clone of themselves in combat. Warbosses (Fighter’s Guild+War College, Cost 120) – Considered as commander unit among goblin, although they have decent fighting capability and number, they don’t have any special fighting ability apart from buffing To-Hit and To-Defend based on number of goblins in the army. Although they could not budding clone, they have ability to regenerate after combat.
PDF page 43 Spider Riders (Smithy+Stable, Cost 80) – Different from most of cavalry type units, Spider Riders don’t have first strike. The role of this unit is mainly an economical version of Giant Spiders with major damage dealing coming from poison and support other units with 1 charge of web. So, this unit serve more as support unit rather than assault one. Tricksters (Town Hall+Alchemist’s Guild, Cost 50) – The first of Goblin’s “wacky” units, Tricksters are an indirect fighters with low melee strength but decent thrown, armor, ability to merge and movement of 3, the unit is designed to hit and run. This unit also has the ability to install trap with fast 2 turns recharge, this allows Tricksters to do indirect fight and harass the enemies. Rabblerousers (Town Hall+Shrine, Cost 65) – This unit is a replacement for shaman as 1 st tier cleric but that could not use healing spell and also politicians instead of clerics. Instead, Rabblerousers have Resistance-for-All +1 and ability to cast a few charges of Blaze of Glory so Rabblerousers are offensive cult leaders that turn cultists into suicide attackers and mitigate effects of magic curses and poison. Hexers (Sage’s Guild+Witches’ Convent, Cost 110) – This unit is a replacement for disciples as 1 st tier spell caster but losing casting skill but gain illusion attack and a few charges of Liability. Although individual figure’s attack power is a bit lower than generic disciples in term of raw strength but higher in figures, illusion attack, and poison ability make their total attack strength decent and prime for buffing. Arsonists (Fighter’s Guild+Library, Cost 60) – This unit is a replacement for shieldbearers in their position in roster but its fighting style is completely different. Instead of fast-moving shielded units, Arsonists are double attackers of both fire breath and melee. This allows Arsonists to able to attack flying units. Main defensive perk of Arsonists are causing fear among enemies by how crazy these pyromaniacs are. Night Goblins (Fighter’s Guild+Miner’s Guild, Cost 90) – This is a replacement for crossbowmen as 2 nd tier physical range attacker but instead focus on attack power of crossbow, Night Goblins focus more on stealth instead with majority of damage coming from poison attack. Mechaniacs (Town Hall+University, Cost 90) – This is a replacement for engineers but does not have ability to build road. Instead, Mechaniacs focus on their role as mechanical unit support with ability to construct field catapult, buff other mechanical units, and heal mechanical units by 1 Health at the end of turn if their Health is below 50%. Poxbearers (Sage’s Guild+Witches’ Convent, Cost 180) – This is one of “wackier” units of Goblin race. Although Poxbearers have decent attack power with secondary attack as Resistance-check attack, their main gimmick is ability to spread plague to the enemy at the beginning of combat (powerful combat global debuff of -3 Attack, -3 Defend, -3 Resistance) at cost of cause minor debuff on their own side. Although its minor debuff on the same side would be removed upon the death of this unit, great debuff on enemy side would go on until the end of combat. Doom Wheels (Fighter’s Guild+Mechanician’s Guild, Cost 140) – This unit is 2 nd tier mechanical light cavalry with very powerful offensive power and speed but paper thin defend with main defensive ability is causing fear and large shield. One of the wackier functions of this unit is that once Health reduces lower than 50% the unit would allowed to use its special red button that would trigger self-destruction and bring serious damage to surrounding enemies and allies. Gliders (Hangar+Alchemist’s Guild, Cost 180) – These fighter-bomber hang-gliders are only flying unit of the Goblin and one of a few mechanical flying units in game. Flying by exploit wind from permanent Guardian Wind enchantment, the gliders are fast moving with strength of attack coming from their bomb and their numbers but almost no protection from anything else apart from small missile by permanent Guardian Wind enchantment. Midget Submarines (Mechanician’s Guild+Shipyard, Cost 250) – This unit is the wackiest unit in Goblin roster. Midget Submarines are small submerging craft armed with torpedoes and protection coming from immunities to different kinds of attacks the unit gains upon submerging. Due to its attack and def need to be submerged, Midget Submarines will not fly (even if have enchantment that grant them flying) in combat if possible. If the unit fought combat overland, if the unit does not have enchantment that grant non-corporeal, the unit would not be able to submerge in combat.
PDF page 44 NEW RACE Hawkmen (Arcanus) Tilted Towards Military Race Characteristics: 40 growth, 0 outpost growth. +0.25max pop per mountain, +1/2 power per population Special Building: Altar of the Sun (required mountain/hill/volcano) Building limitations: Dock and Shipyard, Bank, Stables, City Wall, Fortification, Brewery, Hillfort, Warlord’s Hold Hawkmen is a new race introduced by Warlord mod. Hawkmen are winged humanoid people living in mountainous region of Arcanus. Different from beastmen and other half-animal people, they have 6 limbs. They have strong affinity with primal forces, this makes some scholars consider Hawkmen to be mortal descendents of their heralds. Hawkmen are spiritual but openminded people, this is the only race that could build both temple and cathedral. Hawkmen economic potential is mainly limited to strategies that exploit religious buildings the most. Otherwise, hawkmen could not build any economic buildings beyond basic marketplace and have the lowest fertility rate among Arcanian races. Their military is however formidable. It is the norm rather than exception for female hawkmen to participate in combat. Flying combined with first strike is a great tactical combo and nearly all recruitable units are racial uniques. Hawkmen higher tier units dominate with abilities and special traits as opposed to sheer might and have the only recruitable unit with magic immunity. Normal Units: First Strike, Flying, -1 Figure Spearmen, Swordsmen Generic Mechanical Units: Mountaineer Catapult, Ballista race unit cost Figures Melee throw/breath Range Ammo Armor Resist Health to hit Move Poison ToDefend Hawkman Spearmen 15 7 2 2 3 1 0.3 2 0.3 Hawkman Swordsmen 30 5 4 4 4 1 0.3 2 0.3 Hawkman Harpies 40 5 1 4 3 3 2 4 1 0.3 3 0.3 Hawkman Eagle Warrior 65 5 5 4 5 2 0.3 4 0.3 Hawkman Enchantress 80 3 3 3 6 2 0.3 2 3 0.3 Hawkman Tomahawks 120 5 5 5 6 3 0.3 3 0.3 Hawkman Sirens 180 3 4 4 9 3 0.3 3 3 0.3 Hawkman Huichilobos 230 4 8 3 5 8 4 0.3 3 2 0.3 Hawkman Holy Mothers 330 1 4 15 10 0.4 3 0.4 Hawkmen Sky Lantern 100 1 0.1 9 9 10 3 7 12 0.5 1 0.3
PDF page 45 Special Units: Harpies (cost 40, mill) – A skirmishing unit with range attacks (3 ammo), decent mobility, and high thrown rating. Eagle Warriors (cost 65, armory) – combine the traits of cavalry and halberdier while coming with +1 resistance. Tomahawks (cost 120, fighter's guild) – These are more damaging and durable than Eagle Warriors, but with 1 lower movement point. The high damage potential combined with flying and first strike adds to unit's survivability, although they are vulnerable to ranged attacks. Enchantress (cost 80, sage guild) – Replacement of generic disciples. Althrough they don't use ranged attacks, they can fight properly in melee with poison hex and could curse enemy to unnatural slumber (black sleep) Sky Lantern (Mechanician Guild cost 100) – A 1-figure slow moving unit with good sight, ranged armor piercing attacks, and thrown. Sirens (cost 180, Wizard's Guild) – Supernaturally seductive lady (1 charge of possession) that bring unnatural demise to any who oppose her (death gaze), thus they are particularly dangerous in close combat. Holy Mothers (cost 330, Temple, Cathedral) – Worshipped as goddess on earth. They are excellent healers, could bless allies with much higher resistance, windwalks the army, and have a supernatural immunity to magic. They take prohibitive cost to recruit and they walk the path of non-violence with 0 attack rating, thus their usefulness depends on the armies they support. Huichilobos (cost 230, Armorer's Guild) - elite sacred warriors of Hawkmen society. Dressed as spirits of the sun and armed with poisonous serpentine hooked sword and throwing weaponry. They are immune to fire and death curse and could summon phantom warriors to aid them in battle.
PDF page 46 Buildings: There are new buildings added in Warlord mod. Each races have at least one unique buildings, usually tie to terrain type. Raider races (Barbarian, Gnoll, Troll) gain a few more buildings to support their more warlike activity. Some buildings are available to most of the races Generic Economy Buildings: NEW: Dock (150 Production, 0 Upkeep) requires to construct on coastal city. This building is split up from old Shipyard/Dock and Shipyard. This part of the old building is for access to sea bounty included trade bonus and food generation from each overland water tiles near city with 1 food generate per tile and 2 food for river mouth tile. This building also allows city to build Trireme. Every race except Hawkman could build this building. Marketplace (80 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic economy building. This building serves as a central hub of commerce where additional taxes are easily collected. It produces an additional +7 Gold each turn. All races could access to this building. Bank (200 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Marketplace and University to be constructed. This building enhances a town's commercial operations, boosting Gold income from the city by 30%. Every race except Barbarian, Gnoll, Troll, and Hawkman could build this building. Merchant’s Guild (400 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Bank and Shipyard, and need to be coastal city due to Dock as requirement by extension, to be constructed. This building is a sophisticated and organized hub of prosperity, increasing Gold income from the city by 40%! This building is only available to cities of Beastman, Dark Elf, Draconian, Halfling, High Elf, High Man, Nomad, Orc, Xuanyuan, or Rakhshasa race. Granary (80 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic food and growth building. This building functions as a storage facility for the city's food surplus. It increases Maximum Population by 5 and generates 4 Food. Every race except Nomad could build this building. Farmer's Market (150 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Granary and Marketplace to be constructed. This building serves as a centralized hub for trading the city's food surplus. It accelerates Population Growth by 40 and generates 1 Gold for every two Population Units. Every race except Nomad and Goblin could build this building. Animist’s Guild (240 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Granary and Forester's Guild, which means need forest nearby at point of building Forester's Guild by extension but forest does not requires after Forester's Guild is built, to be constructed. This building increases each Farmer's Food harvest by 2 and enhances the healing rate of units inside the city by 66%. Every race except Goblin and Nomad could build this building. Generic Research Buildings: These buildings generate Research points as main resource. Sage Master retort reduces construction cost of buildings in this category by 15%. Library (80 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic education and research building. This building serves as a repository for knowledge and scholarship. It contributes +4 spell research points. All races could access to this building. All races could access to this building. University (160 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Library, and Town Hall to be constructed. This building stands as a bastion of education and scholarship. It contributes +6 spell Research points. This building is also serve as key buildings to many of higher tier of economy and production related buildings too. Every races except Gnoll, and Troll could access to this building. Sage's Guild (400 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires University, and Alchemist’s Guild to be constructed. This building is dedicated to the advanced study of magic and understanding the universe. It adds +12 spell Research points. Progressing beyond this building tier requires the casting of Tree of Knowledge. Disciples units and magician units of similar class usually required this building to recruit. Every race except Barbarian, Dwarf, Gnoll, and Troll could access to this building.
PDF page 47 Generic Magic Buildings: Magic Market (100 Production, 0 Upkeep) requires Marketplace to be constructed. This building accommodates novice mages practicing witchcraft and selling various talismans. It generates +4 magic Power. Every race except Dwarf could build this building. Wizard's Guild (800 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Magic Market, and Sage’s Guild to be constructed. This building serves as a hub for the study and practice of magic. It enhances magic power by +12 and increases spell research points by +2. This building is also a requirement for recruitment of Magisters and magician units of similar class. Every race except Barbarian, Dwarf, Gnoll, Goblin, and Troll could build this building after casting Tree of Knowledge. Monument (75 Production, 0 Upkeep) is basic casting skill boosting building. This building aids in channeling magical power across distant lands. It enhances combat casting skill by adding +180 SP to a wizard's skill pool. Every race except Dwarf, and Gnoll could build this building. Linking Tower (500 Production, 4 upkeep) requires Monument, and Sage’s Guild to be constructed. This building connects a city to ley lines, facilitating the channeling of magical power across vast distances. It enhances combat casting skill by adding +1200 SP to a wizard's skill pool. Every race except Barbarian, Dwarf, Gnoll, and Troll could build this building after casting Tree of Knowledge. Amplifying Tower (900 Production, 7 upkeep) requires Alchemist’s Guild, and Sage’s Guild to be constructed. This building tunes Aether to facilitate easier spellcasting, increasing Overland Casting Skill by +7. Every race except Barbarian, Dwarf, Gnoll, and Troll could build this building after casting Tree of Knowledge. Generic Religion Buildings: Shrine (120 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic religious building. This building offers spiritual solace to the people of the city. It increases Religious Power by +2 and reduces Unrest by 1 level. All races could access to this building. Monastery (200 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Shrine, and Town Hall to be constructed. This building serves as a central hub for the study and teaching of religion within the city. It adds +4 Religious Power and reduces Unrest by 1. Every race except Barbarian, Gnoll, Goblin, Klackon, and Troll could build this building. Cathedral (500 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Monastery and Town Hall to be constructed. This building represent monotheism and Tolkien’s freepeople races’ religion. It designates the city as the center of worship for the one true divinity. Through its unified and focused faith, a cathedral adds 6 Religious Power and reduces Unrest by 2. This building is only available to cities of Draconian, Dwarf, Halfling, High Elf, High Man, or Hawkman race. NEW: Temple (400 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Monastery and Town Hall to be constructed. This building is represent polytheism and an alternative upgrade of Cathedral for some races. It adds 4 religious Power and reduces Unrest by 1. It also provides an extra 2 religious Power and reduces Unrest by 1 for each Nightshade, Wild Game, and Orihalcon resource available in city’s vicinity. This building is only available to cities of Beastman, Dark Elf, Lizardman, Nomad, Orc, Rakhshasa, or Hawkman race. Oracle (360 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Shrine and Town Hall to be constructed. This building offers the city magical guidance, detecting all enemies within 4 squares and serve as religious building in reducing Unrest by 3. Although this building considered as religious building, it does not generate religious Power. This building could be augmented to generate +4 religious Power under influence of Ruler of Underworld global enchantment. All races could access to this building. All races except Goblin could access to this building. NEW: Witches’ Convent (400 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Shrine and Magic Market to be constructed. This building offers the city magical protections. It generates +4 religious Power, and may curse units that attack the city with common and uncommon curses. Although this building is considered as religious building, it does not offer Unrest reduction. This building is only available to cities of Barbarian, Gnoll, Orc, Troll, and Hawkman race.
PDF page 48 Generic Production Buildings: Smithy (75 Production, 0 Upkeep) is the basic building for city production and military. This building specializes in developing and producing high-quality weaponry and tools, serving as a fundamental building in any town. It generates 3 Production and is essential for producing most military units. Each outpost receives this building for free at time of founding but it could be destroyed and rebuilt. All races could access to this building. Mill (80 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic production building of the city. This building boosts production by relieving farmers' workload, allowing for more productive activities. It increases base Production by 1, with an additional +0.5 for each Farmer population in the city. All races could access to this building. Town Hall (80 Production, 0 Upkeep) is a basic production and civic building of the city. This building serves as the hub of city governance, enabling the construction of advanced knowledge buildings and generating 0.5 production per worker in the city. All races could access to this building. Miner’s Guild (200 Production, 2 Upkeep) is a basic production building of the city. This building educates workers in the intricacies of mining, boosting special mineral bonuses by +50% and production by +25%. Every races except Lizardman could build this building. Mechanician’s Guild (400 Production, 4 Upkeep) requires University and Miner’s Guild to be constructed. This building imparts advanced engineering techniques and enhances the productivity of each worker. It increases city production by 1.5 units of production per worker. Every races except Barbarian, Gnoll, Lizardman, Troll, and Rakhshasa could build this building. Generic Multi-functions Buildings: Forester's Guild (130 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Mill and presence of forest near the city to be constructed. This building trains skilled hunters and lumberjacks, boosting Production by +10% and increasing Food harvest by +4, with an additional +2 for each area of Wild Game in the city's vicinity. All races could access to this building. Alchemist’s Guild (150 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Library to be constructed. This building equips all new troops with magical weapons, increasing their chance To-Hit by +10%. It also enables the use of Mithril, Nightshade, Adamantium, and Orihalcon in the production of troops. Nightshade counters or dispels hostile spells targeting the city with a strength of 100, and enhances the effects of Temple. This building could be augmented by Philosopher’s Stone city enchantment to generate 12 Gold. Every race except Barbarian could build this building. Coliseum (250 Production, 0 Upkeep) requires Barracks and Fighter’s Guild to be constructed. This building entertains the population, reducing Unrest by 1 and increasing Fame by 5. Every races except Halfling, and Klackon could build this building. NEW: Brewery (200 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Farmer’s Market and Town Hall to be constructed. This building consumes food equal to 50% of population units in the city, and +25% if the city has a Dock, and convert them into Gold at rate 3 gold per unit of food consume this way. This building is also reduce unrest in the city by 1. This building is only available to cities of Barbarian, Dwarf, Gnoll, Goblin, or Troll race. NEW: Warlord’s Hold (400 Production, 5 Upkeep) requires Town Hall and War College to be constructed. This building reduces the cost to recruit new units from the city by 25% and doubles the strength of garrison units in reducing Unrest (1 unit per -1 unrest compared to normally 2 units per -1 unrest). For Wizard who start the game with Barbarian, Gnoll or Troll (so called ‘Raiders Races’) as starting race, This building grants garrison strength of 12 units distribute among cities under wizard’s control that does not have Warlord’s Hold. This building is only available to cities of Barbarian, Gnoll, Goblin, or Troll race.
PDF page 49 Generic Military Buildings: They are generally 20-30% more expensive to build than in Caster of Magic but their upkeep costs are cheaper. Warlord retort reduces construction cost of these buildings by 15%. NEW: Armory (150 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Smithy to be constructed and is a prerequisite for Barracks and Fighter’s Guild. This building serves as gap between Smithy and Fighter’s Guild from Classic Master of Magic is now coming back requirement for Halberdiers level units once again. All races could access to this building. Barracks (200 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Armory to be constructed and is a prerequisite for Coliseum and War College. This building enable a city to train and organize regular military units. Without barracks, a city can't train regular military units. All units created in the town gain +1 Level. Every races except Halfling could build this building. War College (540 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Barracks and Fighter’s Guild to be constructed. This building functions as a hub for teaching battle strategy, tactics, and advanced fighting techniques. All new troops begin as Veterans. This building is also serve as requirement replacement for elite units of raider races that could not build Armorer’s Guild. Every races except Halfling could build this building. Fighter's Guild (200 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Armory to be constructed and is a prerequisite for Coliseum, War College, Maritime Guild, Armorer’s Guild, and Fantastic Stable. This building trains soldiers and unlocks superior unit types (Shieldbearers and their equivalents). Progressing beyond this building tier requires casting the Tree of Knowledge spell. All races could access to this building. Armorer's Guild (600 Production, 4 Upkeep) requires Smithy, and Fighter’s Guild to be constructed. This building represents the pinnacle of the race's military technology, providing troops with training in advanced fighting techniques and basic battle tactics, enabling the construction of even more sophisticated units. Every races except Barbarian, Gnoll, Goblin, and Halfling could build this building after casting Tree of Knowledge.. Stables (120 Production, 2 Upkeep) requires Smithy to be constructed. This building serve as breeding grounds for mounts used by mounted troops, enhancing productivity. They generate +4 Production. Every races except Dwarf could build this building. Fantastic Stables (750 Production, 4 Upkeep) requires Stable, and Fighter’s Guild to be constructed. This building houses and cares for magical beasts, training them to be mounted for warfare. This building is a requirement for flying mounted units for race that could not naturally fly. This building is only available to cities of Beastman, Dark Elf, Halfling, High Elf, Nomad, Orc, Xuanyuan, or Rakhshasa race after casting Tree of Knowledge. Shipyard (300 Production, 1 Upkeep) requires Dock to be constructed. This building is an upgrade split from old Dock and Shipyard. This building is a requirement for the city to build more powerful ships. Every race except Hawkman and Lizardman could build this building. Maritime Guild (450 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Shipyard, and Fighter’s Guild to be constructed. This building facilitates the construction of large ships through training, organization, and support for experienced shipbuilders. This building is a requirement for the Warship and other ships of similar class. This building is only available to cities of Barbarian, Draconian, Dwarf, Halfling, High Man, Nomad, Orc, or Xuanyuan race after casting Tree of Knowledge. NEW: Hangar (400 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Sage’s Guild and Mechanician’s Guild to be constructed. This building is a requirement for mechanical flying units. This building is only available to cities of Draconian, Goblin, or Hawkman race after casting Tree of Knowledge.
PDF page 50 Defensive Structures: City Walls (90 Production, 1 Upkeep) is a basic city defending structure. This building is surrounding the city with a tall brick wall that extends the detection range of enemy units to 3 squares. Units positioned behind the wall gain +3 Armor. If a wall segment is destroyed, this bonus reduces to +1 Armor. The defending side can use the Disrupt spell to demolish the wall for emergency exits, provided the unit does not already have a spell charge assigned. Every race except Hawkman could build this building. NEW: Hillfort (300 Production, 3 Upkeep) requires Miner’s Guild and Stable to be constructed. This building grants impassable rock cliff face to the city that could not be cross except by Non-Corporeal unit except 4 access points on each side of the city. The friendly units receive Missile Immunity if the units stay inside city area. This building is only available to cities of Barbarian, Gnoll, Troll, or Hawkman race. NEW: Fortification (600 Production, 5 Upkeep) requires City Wall and Mechanician’s Guild to be constructed. This building grants moat to the city with water terrain that could not cross except with flying or amphibious units surrounding the city wall except two bridge locations. Friendly units receive bonus equivalent to Large Shield if they stay inside the city wall area. If the unit already have Large Shield, unit will receive Missile Immunity instead. This building is only available to cities of Beastman, Dark Elf, Dwarf, Halfling, High Elf, High Man, Klackon, Orc, or Xuanyuan race after casting Tree of Knowledge. PDF page 51 New Racial Unique Buildings: Altar of Storm (600 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Barbarian’s unique building that requires Witches’ Convent and shore nearby the city to be constructed. This building grants the city 8 religious power, and all new units trained in the city gain the Lightning Blade ability. In combat, the city is protected by a Lightning Storm combat enchantment. Idol of Heavenly Bull (1200 Production, 20 Upkeep) is Beastman’s unique building that requires Monastery and desert nearby the city to be constructed. This building is a significant cult statue revered in beastman culture. Each worker unit generates 1 food and can receive bonuses from the Animist's Guild. Additionally, all new units trained in the city gain a 25% increase in Health Points, with a minimum of 1 additional Health Point. Tree of Magic (1200 Production, 20 Upkeep) is Dark Elf’s unique building that requires Wizard’s Guild and forest nearby the city to be constructed. This building grants newly trained units with Casting Skill equal to their base magical Resistance plus base Magic Range Attack at moment they are recruited and all Magic Ranged units gain +2 Ammo. Dragon Mound (1200 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Draconian’s unique building that requires Stable and hill/mountain/volcano nearby the city to be constructed. This building serves as a crucial site for the Draconians to enhance their dragon powers through communion with the mother drake. Newly trained units from the city receive significant benefits: they gain +2 Fire Breath and +1 Armor. Additionally, the mother drake's hoard also serves as an additional Bank, providing provide gold equal to 30% of base Gold generate in the city. Lava Smelter (1200 Production, 20 Upkeep) is Dwarf’s unique building that requires Alchemist’s Guild and hill/mountain/volcano nearby the city to be constructed. This building accesses rare minerals by smelting lava from deep veins beneath hills and mountains. It generates 15 Power and enhances the level of magic weapon upgrades. At level 1, upgrades Magic weapon into Mithril weapon. At level 2, upgrades Mithril weapon into Adamantium weapon. At level 3, upgrades Adamantium weapon by give additional Orihalcon upgrade. Combination of mineral near the city is also grant unit ability. Mithril plus Adamantium grants Weapon Immunity. Mithril plus Crysx grants Missile Immunity. Mithril plus Orihalcon grants permanent Resist Element. Adamantium plus Orihalcon grants permanent Elemental Armor. Adamantium plus Crysx grants permanent Flame Blade. During a siege, the city gains the Wall of Fire enchantment from the outset. Altar of the Moon (600 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Gnoll’s unique building that requires Witches’ Convent and swamp nearby the city to be constructed. This building grants the city 8 religious power, all new units gain Poison Immunity, Rage ability. All ranged units get +2 Ranged Attack. Hunters unit gains Poison 2. And Witchdoctors unit has Lifesteal -1 replacing its Poison attack. In combat, the city is protected by greater curses. Academy (1200 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Halfling’s unique building that requires Monastery and hill/mountain/volcano nearby the city to be constructed. This building is a school dedicated to the study, discussion, and application of cutting-edge knowledge for public benefit. It provides research based on the maximum population size, reduces population decrease rate by half, and lowers the cost of ship and siege units by 25%. Tree of Life (800 Production, 20 Upkeep) is High Elf’s unique building that requires Animist’s Guild and forest nearby the city to be constructed. This building accelerates population growth by +100 per month, provides food equal to the maximum population unit, and grants Regeneration 0 to all defending units in combat that do not already possess it. It also reduces Unrest by 50% if Wizard's home race is High Elf. Sancta Basilica (2400 Production, 20 Upkeep) is High Man’s unique building that requires Cathedral and desert nearby the city to be constructed. This building is housing sacred relics of past Avatars, generates religious power equal to the city's maximum population unit. All units trained here gain +3 Resistance. Clergy, crusaders, and paladins receive Sanctify. Crusaders also gain Lucky, paladins gain Magic Immunity, and clergy gain improved Exorcise but at higher cost. In combat, the city is blessed by True Light. Undercity Hive Network (1200 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Klackon’s unique building that requires Town Hall and Mechanician’s Guild to be constructed. This building is an underground settlement and tunnel network directly beneath the Klackon city. It supports 30% more population capacity but also adds +1 Unrest. Defending units can move swiftly through the underground tunnels for tactical advantage as if they have Merging ability.
PDF page 52 Baray (1000 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Lizardman’s unique building that requires Monastery and river nearby the city to be constructed. This building is an advanced water system that transforms a dry city into a water paradise for the Lizardmen. It generates Gold equal to the city's maximum population, reduces Unrest by -2. Newly trained ground units from this city gain Amphibious and Mariner. In combat, the city area becomes water, granting all friendly units the ability Amphibious. Caravanserai (400 Production, 3 Upkeep) is Nomad’s unique building that requires Town Hall and desert nearby the city to be constructed. This building serves as a crucial station for caravans traversing the desert, boosting Gold income equivalent to the base trade bonus generated by the city without Nomad bonus. Units trained in this city, excluding sailing units, gain +2 Overland Movement. Ludus Agoge (1200 Production, 20 Upkeep) is Orc’s unique building that requires War College and desert nearby the city to be constructed. This building is an elite school that uses rigorous methods and supplements to enhance children's performance. The city gains +15 Research points, and new units gain +1 Attack, Resistance, and Health, except Legionary units, which gain +1 Movement. Frost Club Hall (600 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Troll’s unique building that requires Brewery and tundra nearby the city to be constructed. This building aims to restore the prestige and secrets of the Frost Club clan. Newly trained War Mammoths gain Regeneration 1, and other Troll units gain Cold Immunity and double their regeneration strength. Military Workshop (1200 Production, 20 Upkeep) is Xuanyuan’s unique building that requires Mechanician’s Guild and river nearby to be constructed. This building enables Xuanyuan units to utilize their advanced military missile technology. All units receive +2 to Physical Ranged, Fire Breath, and Thrown attacks if they possess those types of attacks, along with a +1 bonus to Poison attacks. Units equipped with Small Physical Ranged projectiles have them upgraded to gunpowder-infused missiles (Heavy Physical Ranged) instead. Pool of Repentance (1200 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Rakhshasa’s unique building that requires Monastery and forest nearby to be constructed. This building is a revered site where rituals of absolution take place. The Pool of Repentance generates 1 Production for each unit of farmers, reduces Unrest by -3 as a religious building, and grants new units produced in the city +1 Armor and +1 Resistance. Altar of the Sun (600 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Hawkman’s unique building that requires Witches’ Convent and hill/mountain/volcano nearby the city to be constructed. This building grants the city 8 religious power, +100 Population Growth per turn, and all new units except Holy Mother trained in the city gain +1 Figure. In combat, the city is protected by a High Prayer. Mother Fungus (1200 Production, 10 Upkeep) is Goblin’s unique building that Witches’ Convent and swamp nearby the city to be constructed. Goblins all new units gain +2 Attack, +10% to-Defend, Poison 1, and x2 Spellcharge. Additionally, it is detecting all enemies within 10 squares.
PDF page 53 Heroes: To summarize, changes often revolve around making hero stats and abilities fit the theme of races. Discovery is more exciting than listing all stat changes. One major overall change is heroes starting with base 40% to hit as a minimum, with some lower stats, particularly in range, to compensate. Beastmaster had its fame requirement increased to 10, preventing every single wizard tower to be protected by a beastmaster hero. Hero Experience: +5% to hit earned in level 4, level 6, level 8 and level 9 (instead of +10% earned in level 5 and 9) There's 3 heroes that have unusual item slot configurations: Gunther with 2 swords and no shield, and war monk and bronze sentinel with no wand/sword (2 accessory slots) 12 heroes have been added: Sagittarius, Crone, Grand Inquisitor, Dwarven Steelbreaker, Elven Dreamwalker, Halfling Gambler, Gnoll Warmaster, Swarm Queen, King of the Deep, Troll War Chief, Planewalker, Elementalist Item Costs have been modified to be lower for weakest effects but become more incremental, to balance against the 'complexity' cost adjustment formula that encourages fewer traits for cost effectiveness. This should decrease the cost of effects such as +1-2 attack/armor/hp/etc, thus a mixture of weak effects should be similarly priced than a single stronger effect. Some item ability costs have been adjusted with a few overpriced elements addressed in this mod. Unfortunately the 'spell charges' continues having a linear cost and being too cheap for advanced spells. Attack 50-100-150-250-400-650 - Armor: 75-150-225-375 (Armor caps at +4 for items with just +2 with create item). - Movement: 250-500-1000 - Resistance: 100-200-300-400-500-600 - Spell Skill: 75-150-225-375 - Spell Save: 200-400-800-1600 - Health: 75-150-300-500-850-1300 - Item flaming ability cost change to 200 - Item destruction ability cost change to 400 - Item wraithform ability cost change to 250 and nolonger and can add with enchant item - Item bless ability cost change to 150 - Item ability lionheart rename to mystic power, cost increase to 2000 and nolonger need life book - Item water walking ability cost change to 75 - Item pathfinding ability cost change to 100 - Item resist element ability cost change to 150 - Item regeneration ability cost change to 1000 - Item guardian wind ability cost change to 150 - Item teleporting ability cost change to 900 - Item amplifier ability cost change to 300 - Healing Aura can be added to artifacts at 700 cost - Binder (spell lock) can be added to artifacts at 700 cost and requires 7 Sorcery books - Sacred (chosen) can be added to artifacts at 1800 cost and requires 7 Life books - Colossal Power (iron skin & colossal strength) can be added to artifacts at 1200 cost and requires 5 Nature books - Chaos Conduit (blazing march & beat of swiftness) can be added to artifacts at 1200 cost and requires 7 Chaos books - Plague Lord (causes plague) can be added to artifacts at 1500 cost and requires 7 Death books - Eye of Storm (lightning storm & hurricane & freezing rain) can be added to artifacts at 1500 cost and requires 7 Nature books
PDF page 54 Spell Changes, Comments: Larger land sizes have a cost modifier to global-type spells (increase) Larger land sizes have a small cost modifier to localized spells such as unit/city enchantments (decrease) There have been changes and additions to give each magic realm more of an identity and playing style. Note that earliest summons have been all weakened overall and early uncommons now come with higher research cost. This was done to balance the normal vs fantastic power balance throughout the game, particularly to address the slower city progression in this mod. Common summons are the least effective tier and may appear more like being support as opposed to playing entirely with summons (unless conjurer trait), requiring player to advance to next tier ASAP. Note that strength of magic attacks are now based on 60% hit chance, rather than 30%. Common tier spell research costs reduced among spells costing 260 or more, reducing overall research cost of a realm's 10 commons from 3140 to 2880 (-8%) Common tier spell research costs shifted around to emphasize strength of certain spells, while staying within the grand total sum of 2880. Note that you have 12 uncommon spells and 16 rare spells to choose from, +2 and +4 for each of these tiers, respectively. In the case of rare-tier spells, arrows are provided to scroll up and down during the 10-book 'early rare' selection.

PDF page 59 Arcane (Generic): Overall trade value of Arcane spells is decreased due to no wizard that would miss these spells and they would have those spell sooner or later. Magic Spirit (cost -/30, 1 upkeep) – the most basic summoning magic, the same as Caster of Magic for Windows. Summoning Circle (cost -/0) – Although spell itself is the same as before except for lower trade value (reduced from 9 to 6), it is no longer guaranteed as early spell for research anymore. This made early gain of this spell by Conjurer retort more powerful. Heroic Heart (cost 18/-) – 240 research cost (from 440) – we can't justify such an investment for a healing spell with ½ the efficiency of life's healing and only limited to heroes. This deserves an average common-tier cost. Dispel Magic (cost 10+/-) – 320 research cost (from 640) – there needs to be a counter to mega-buffing multi- figure units early in game, especially in a mod that further encourages buffing normal units. As a result, it was needed to make dispel magic easily accessible and worth researching early in game. Enchant Item (cost -/0+) – the spell has lower trade value from Caster of Magic version (from 11 to 9) and research cost increases to 400 (from 320). The strength of this spell is depending on built the wizards have. Detect Magic (cost -/200, 3 upkeep) – the spell is lower in trade value (from 11 to 6) but with more expensive research cost as this spell could be the most important or something you free to ignore depending on what spells and built the wizards have. Spell of Return (cost -/1000) – free spell you have from the start in Caster of Magic although it is recognized as uncommon spell. This spell is a failsafe that as player would not want to be in situation that need this spell but by having it is still much better than not. So giving it for free is more like helping AI than helping player. Disenchant Area (cost -/50+, 0 upkeep) – The spell is more or less the same except lower in trade value (from 19 to 17) and some AI behavior about researching it. Summon Hero (cost -/240) – Trade value of the spell is decreased (from 24 to 20). Tree of Knowledge (cost -/250) – research cost is increased significantly (from 180 to 2000) due to the city pacing adjustments (see buildings section) and the more advanced nature of top-tier military units (see military section, race section), Tree of Knowledge had to be delayed. The higher one-time upfront cost was a preferred choice over making each of the unlocked buildings take too long to build. Tree of Knowledge unlocks Armorer's Guild, Fantastic Stables, Maritime's Guild, Wizard's Guild, Hangar, Linking Towers, Amplifying Tower, and racial unique buildings. Resurrection (cost -/35, 0 upkeep) – shifted from Life uncommon to arcane rare with 3200 research cost. This allows all wizards an option to resurrect their fallen hero, but the investment cost is high. Summon Champion (cost -/600) – trade value of this spell is decreased a bit (from 30 to 28) as there are more powerful champions to summon but result is also much less reliable as well. Create Artifact (cost -/0+) – although spell is the same but there are more artifacts ability that could be created in Warlord mod to design your own custom-made artifacts. Disjunction (cost -/375+, 0 upkeep) – this spell is more valuable than in Caster of Magic in term of trade value (from 28 increases to30) as there are more crazy global enchantment that you would want to get rid off here. Plane Shift (cost -/120, 0 upkeep) – Research cost down to 6000 (from 8000) Spell of Mastery (cost -/9000+map scaling) – research cost of the spell is lower (from 440000 to 330000) and arrives a bit earlier to shake things up earlier in game and takes fewer turns to cast, helping put an end to a long game. Note: Enlightenment spell, which was used to rush-research spell of mastery, was redesigned.
PDF page 60 Arcane (Retort Exclusive): Here are spells which only available to wizard with specific retort. Spells could not be trade or discover in lair, and have to be research normally to get them. Wizard could get more of them researchable if they earn new retort during the game. NEW: Philosopher’s Stone (cost -/210, 7 upkeep) – Split from old sorcery’s Philosopher’s Stone with all economic part with additional abilities to enchant physical Alchemist’s Guild to generate 12 gold and add mineral level in place without required mineral. This spell is only available to Alchemist retort holder. NEW: Education Reform (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All research buildings now generate gold equal to their upkeep cost. War College also generates additional 2 Research points. This spell is only available to Sage Master retort holder. NEW: Arcane Conference (cost -/800, 10 upkeep) – This allow Sage Master to earn additional research from their own fortress city, +1 for each Library, +2 for each University, +3 for each Sage’s Guild of both planes. This spell is only available to Sage Master retort holder. NEW: Wall of Stone (cost -/100, 10 upkeep) – The spell is not only placing physical City Wall, but also enhanced it to refund their gold upkeep and restore it at the end of opponent turn. But if it destroy in owner turn, the enchantment will be removed at the end of turn. This spell is only available to Warlord retort holder. NEW: Mark of Conqueror (cost -/300, 10 upkeep) – The spell is not only placing physical Warlord’s Hold, but also enhanced it to refund their gold upkeep and restore it at the end of opponent turn. But if it destroy in owner turn, the enchantment will be removed at the end of turn. This spell is only available to Warlord retort holder. NEW: Astral Gate (cost -/500, 10 upkeep) – Difference from original version in Master of Magic, this Astral Gate is one-way portal to other realm. Make sure you could establish outpost on other side for another gate to travel back. This spell is only available to Myrran retort holder. NEW: Tactical Drill (cost -/60, 0 upkeep) – Repurpose discipline spell, now it is only castable outside combat. This spell is only available to Tactician retort holder. NEW: Tactical Recall (cost 30/-) – Instant spell that allow target unit to escape combat and return with full health…. if the caster won the combat. If the combat is lost, the recalled unit also destroyed. This spell is only available to Tactician retort holder. NEW: Strategic Recall (cost -/100) – Instantly teleport target unit to the Tactician’s fortress. This spell is only available to Tactician retort holder. NEW: Marionette (cost -/100) – Summon special hero (the wanderer) at cheap cost and get it early. Hero ability is customized base on caster’s ability. The hero might not strong but hero could always be resummon after irrecoverably destroyed and could not permanently die. The spell will temporarily disable if the caster has Wanderer marionette alive under control. This spell is only available to Channeler retort holder. NEW: Marionette Ascension (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Upgrade the wanderer hero even further based on ability of the caster. The wanderer also get stronger as the caster get stronger. This spell is only available to Channeler retort holder. NEW: Lord Liberator (reform, effect taken upon researched) – When ever the wizard attack city with race the same as the wizard own home race or one of the races the Guardian wizard rules over, defender suffer -1 Attack/Armor/Resistance. This spell is only available to Guardian retort holder. NEW: Lord Protector (reform, effect taken upon researched) – This reform allows guardian retort bonus to extend to all defending combat. This spell is only available to Guardian retort holder. Earth Gate Town Portal (cost -/125, 1 upkeep) – Move from Nature realm to Arcane for sake of quality of life in managing empire in large map. The enchantment is also eliminates gold 'indirect control' penalty of non-capital cities that get enchanted. This spell is only available to Procurator retort holder.
PDF page 61 NEW: Archmage Tutition (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Reform allows all magic user units trained from fortress city get enhanced in casting skill, spell charge, and ammo if unit have any of these features. This spell is only available to Archmage retort holder. NEW: Archmage Guidance (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Reform gives all heroes under the Archmage wizard to get +40 casting skill. This also applies to heroes who could not casting spell before. This spell is only available to Archmage retort holder. NEW: Bountiful Festivity (cost -/75, 2 upkeep) – Alternative spell for population growth and reducing unrest. This spell is only available to Benefactor retort holder. NEW: Gospel of Evangelism (cost -/100, 0 upkeep) – Special city curse available to Cult Leader. Garrison units and city produced less Religious Power depend on Unrest in the city. The more unrest mean the city produce less power and easy to fall before might of the Cult Leader. This spell is only available to Cult Leader retort holder. NEW: Divine Judgement (cost -/1000) – Replacement of Final Wave and Great Unsummoning but instead of kill indiscriminately, it only damage units under single wizard. This spell is only available to Cult Leader retort holder. NEW: Clockwork Tinmen (cost -/120, 5 upkeep) – Summon mechanical engineer unit that could build road very fast and buff mechanical unit in combat. It ables to destroy any mechanical unit in single hit with its special ability. This spell is only available to Artificer retort holder. NEW: Clockwork Factory (cost -/200, 4 upkeep) – Put magical automate factory into the city operate with magical power and generate 50 production per turn. This spell is only available to Artificer retort holder. NEW: Rebuild (cost -/150, 0 upkeep) – Permanent unit enchantment that turn unit into mechanical unit with +2 Melee/Armor, Death and Illusion immunity, as well as armor piercing. This spell is only available to Artificer retort holder. NEW: Lucky Star (cost 35/-) – Combat unit enchantment that grant Lucky to target unit until the end of combat and while Lucky Star still presence in combat, all friendly units get +1 Attack/Armor/Resistance until Lucky Star is removed from the game. Effect of multiple Lucky Star enchantments are not stacked. This spell is only available to Astrologer retort holder. NEW: Dishearten Prophesy (cost -/100, 1 upkeep) – Special city curse available to Astrologer. City suffers +4 unrest and garrisons suffer -2 Resistance in combat. This spell is only available to Astrologer retort holder. NEW: Conjuring Pact (cost 40/-) – Attempts to tame fantastic creature. If non-fantastic creature get hit by this would suffer nausea (-10 To-Hit/To-Defend). If tamed fantastic creature survive the combat, Conjurer could research how to summon them if their realm proficieny is high enough (at least twice of normal rarity level). This spell is only available to Conjurer retort holder. NEW: Spirit Link (cost -/150, 0 upkeep) – Turn unit into non-fantastic creature while still able to receive bonus as if they are fantastic creatures and get additional +2 Resistance. Unit that originally don’t have experience level now also able to gain experience level and could be enchanted with normal unit enchantment while unable to be targeted by spell that only affects fantastic creature. This spell is only available to Conjurer retort holder. NEW: Rally (cost 15/-) – All friendly unit get +2 Resistance until the end of combat. This spell is only available to Charismatic retort holder. NEW: Denoucement (cost -/200) – Deal damage to reputation of the wizard who own target city and reduces their standing among the wizard. This spell is only available to Charismatic retort holder. NEW: Whispering Echo (cost 150/-) – Attempts to convince all opponents units in combat to switch side or at least sows discord and confusion among them. Strength of the spell depend on caster has Charismtic or Charming or not. This spell is only available to Charismatic retort holder.
PDF page 62 NEW: Tattoo Magic (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Reform allows all newly trained unit with non- permanent enchantment to become permanent enchantment and could not be dispelled. When casting overland common unit enchantment, the spell become permanent on the enchanted unit. This spell is only available to Enchanter retort holder. NEW: Domain of Enchanter (cost -/800, 10 upkeep) – This global enchantment enhances dispel resistance of all enchantment of the caster twice its strength. All unit curses cast by the Enchanter will become permanent and would not dispelled at the end of combat. This spell is only available to Enchanter retort holder. NEW: Tabula Rasa (cost 100/-) – This combat enchantment will removed enemy’s combat enchantments again and again at chance of 33% at the beginning of the Caster’s turn. This spell is only available to Runemaster retort holder. NEW: Rune Formation Array (cost -/1200, 100 upkeep) – This spell is repurposed of Caster of Magic’s original Power Link. The size of battery is now reduced to 5000. This spell is only available to Runemaster retort holder.
PDF page 63 Arcane (Outlander’s technology) NEW: Crop Rotation (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Each farmer unit generates +1 Food and the City generates food equal to 50% of city's theoretical Overfarming penalty. NEW: Fertilizer (reform, effect taken upon researched) – The City generates food equal to 50% of food output after Overfarming penalty. NEW: Concrete Construction (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Building cost -20% from base cost. NEW: Standardization (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Building cost -10% from base cost. Unit training cost -10% from base cost. Increase Gold bonus from trade by 10%. NEW: Advanced Mining (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Gold and Production bonus from non-magical mineral resources increase by 100%. NEW: Industrialization (reform, effect taken upon researched) – The city gets +5% Production for each Marketplaces, Bank, Guilds, and Production buildings. NEW: Printing Press (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All buildings that generate Research generate +2 Research points. NEW: Bureaucratic Reform (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Reduces city's corruption penalty by 20%. This reduction occurs before corruption cap is applied. NEW: Xenopsychology (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Each Non-Religious Unrest reduction building reduces unrest by +3. In combat, all regular units own by the outlander gain +1 Resistance. NEW: Scientific Process (reform, effect taken upon researched) – The City generates +25% of total Research point. NEW: Radio (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Reduces corruption cap to 20%. All cities get +20% Gold from Trade bonus. In combat, all regular units under the outlander's control gain +10% To-Hit, +10% To-Defend, +1 Resistance. NEW: Corperate Charter (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All cities get +0.5/1.0/1.5% Trade bonus for each Marketplace/Bank/ Merchant's Guild own by the outlander. NEW: Sanitation Reform (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Population growth of city or outpost +40 and reduces population loss in cities or outposts by 25%. NEW: Hospital & Surgery (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Population growth of city or outpost +40. All regular units gain Healer perk. NEW: Strategic Logistic (reform, effect taken upon researched) – The city could train units as if have Iron, Coal, Mithril, Adamantium, Orihalcon, Quork, or Crysx in vicinity at half resource unit as long as the outlander hold city with these resources. This effect does not cover city enchantment and global enchantment. NEW: Upgrade & Retrain (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Old units will receive viable permanent unit upgrade available by accessable technology at the end of turn. This reform allows implement upgrade from spell Archmage's Tutition, and Mariner Mastery, as well as upgrade from buildings Lava Smelter, Baray, and Caravanserai. If the unit does not have racial upgrade, this reform allows implementation of an upgrade from Altar of Storm, or Academy. NEW: Heat Power Engine (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All base production buildings in the city generate +6 production and +3 more production if the city has access to Coal. All newly trained mechanical units coming with Power Engine permanent unit enchantment (+1 Movement speed).
PDF page 64 NEW: Explosive (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Double Miner's Guild's output. In combat, Melee or Flying Regular units or Mechanical units or Sapiens summons gain Thrown ability at strength equal to 8- (maximum figures/2) round down. In combat, all Blackpowder units get +2 Range Attack strength and strength of Fire Breath is doubled. NEW: Ballistics Training (reform, effect taken upon researched) – In combat, all Regular units and Sapiens summons get +20% Range/Breath/Thrown To-Hit. NEW: Conscription (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Unit training cost -20% from base cost. NEW: Military Drilling (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All newly trained Regular units gain Discipline permanent unit enchantment. Mechanical units gain +3 Health each turn if unit's Health is lower than 50%. NEW: Rocketry (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All newly trained Regular units with Physical Ranged Attack or Thrown or Fire Breath gain Blackpowder weapon upgrade. NEW: Armorclad (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All newly trained Regular mechanical units gain Armorclad permanent unit enchantment (+6 Armor). In combat, all Regular non-Mechanical units gain Battle Armor perk (+3 Armor). NEW: Magical Physics (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Fire, Lightning, Cold, Poison, Non-Magical direct damage spell deals Non-Magical damage of the same element at 50% strength on their primary target. NEW: Techno-Geomancy (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Double casting skill output from Monument, Linking Tower, Amplifying Tower. NEW: Magitek Science (reform, effect taken upon researched) – +100% resource output for Mithril, Adamantium, Quork, Crysx, and Orihalcon. Unit with Armorclad or Battle Armor gains Resist Magic unit enchantment. NEW: Magitek Engineering (reform, effect taken upon researched) – City under the outlander's control convert 20% of Production output to generate additional power at ratio 3:1. In combat, unit with Power Engine upgrade get additional +2 Movement Speed, +20% To-Defend, and Large Shield. NEW: Xenoveterinary (reform, effect taken upon researched) – In combat, fantastic creatures get +10% To-Hit, +25% Health (but not lower than +1). All fantastic creatures could access to Armorclad upgrade if Obsolescence Rearmament has been researched. NEW: Temporal Engineering (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All units with Power Engine upgrade gains Haste. All sailing movement units with Power Engine upgrade gains Flying, Illusion Immunity, and units transport by them gain Stealth. NEW: Energy Beam Weapons (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Convert projectile of all ranged units with Power Engine upgrade to beam energy, gains +50% Ranged Attack strength and deals Doom damage and triggers Destruction with save penalty -1 for each 15% of Ranged To-Hit. In combat, all regular/Armorclad units’ Melee Attack deals Doom damage. NEW: Psycho Converter (reform, effect taken upon researched) – In combat, all regular/Armorclad units gain To-Hit and To-Defend percent equal to half of Resistance multiplies with unit Level, round down. NEW: Pneuma Reactor (reform, effect taken upon researched) – All Undead units gain permanent Bloodlust at the end of Overland turn. In combat, all regular/Armorclad units gain Life Steal with strength equal to half of base Resistance.
PDF page 65 Nature: Nature realm is about adaptability and making the best of the world terrain and minerals. If playing a mono-realm wizard, Nature is the least specialized realm. However, the player is more likely to have the necessary tools to do an adequate job on most circumstances. There have been some additions to unit, city and global enchantments with direct or indirect boosts to unit recruitment strategies, thus conjurer is no longer a near-mandatory retort for nature players. New spells further establish these realm characteristics. Removed Nature Spells Fairy Dust – To emphasize realm uniqueness of chaos, removed this spell as researchable but still using by Sacred Ancient (see uncommon spell below). This spell was potentially more damaging than fireball! Nature creature casters can still cast fairy dust. Earth Gate Town Portal (cost -/125, 1 upkeep) – Move to Procurator’s signature. The spell is replacing by new global enchantment “Ice Age” Nature Common Spells Earth Lore (cost -/10) – Same as in vanilla Caster of Magic for Windows Nature's Eye Nature's Witness (cost -/35, 0 upkeep) – In addition to current effects, grants 4 power and -1 unrest If nightshade present. Water Walking (cost -/20, 0 upkeep) – Research cost decreases from 260 to 240. Earth to Mud (cost 20/-) – Research cost increases from 280 to 380. Wild Boars (cost 15/-, 1 upkeep) – Research cost increases from 280 to 320. War Bears (cost -/65, 2 upkeep) – Now with 2 figures and higher cost, but with increased melee and hp per figure. NEW: Sprites Killer Wasps (cost -/55, 1 upkeep) – replaces sprites and maintain a role of being a particularly good unit against lairs/nodes/neutrals but unreliable against wizards. Wasps have useful early perks like 9- figures, missile immunity, and high armor (with 1hp) allowing it to reroll armor every time it loses 1 hp. It benefits greatly from melee and hp buffs. With base stats, it is mainly a low-damaging annoyance that also serves as a counter against bowmen. The unit has been revisited due to claims that it is overpowered. War Bears are more reliable, but wasps have more potential under the right circumstances. Resist Elements (cost 5/25, 0 upkeep) – Research cost decreases from 440 to 320. Web (cost 10/-) – Research cost decreases from 480 to 400. NEW: Survival of The Fittest Natural Selection (cost -/150, 3 upkeep) – Global Common - Units trained gain bonus based on resources in the recruiting town's surroundings including coal (+1 melee), iron (+1 armor), wild games (+1 ranged attack and gain forester), nightshade (+1 resistance). And power minerals (+1 resist per 10 base power income from minerals). This replaces 'fairy dust' and is more consistent with Nature's theme of benefiting from terrain. NEW: Wargs (cost -/64, 1 upkeep) – This spell could only be learned with Conjuring Pact and 2 Nature spell books. NEW: Sprites (cost -/70, 2 upkeep) – This spell could only be learned with Conjuring Pact and 2 Nature spell books.
PDF page 66 Nature Uncommon Spells Land Linking → Nature Link (cost 13/65, 1 upkeep) – Renamed from Land Linking. Spell is castable in combat and also grants an additional +1 resistance to the enchanted unit (whether normal or fantastic). Rush-research can be a beneficial tactic. NEW: Venom (cost 12/60 1 upkeep) – Uncommon – target unit gains poison immunity and +1 poison. Please note that poison can trigger during ranged and thrown attacks, thus you have a chance of inflicting poison twice when attacking or once from a distance. The poison immunity benefit may be what draws you to this spell, especially early in game as your low-resistance units get damaged too easily by too-common sources of poison. Giant Spiders (cost -/110, 2 upkeep) – The unit, while costlier, comes with an extra charge of 'web', greatly expanding its use as a support unit throughout the game. Early uncommon summon strategies weakened to make normal units more relevant, thus spider's research cost has been more than doubled. Change Terrain (cost -/28) – Research cost increases from 960 to 1000. Nature’s Cure (cost -/50) – Research cost decreases from 1280 to 1100. Ice Bolt (cost 24/-) – Now spell’s cost reduces from 25 to 24 so the spell can be accessed by ultra elite caster 20 units. Strength of attack reduces by half (from 34 to 17) but double hit chance (30% to 60%). Trade value is also increased. Cockatrices (cost -/150, 4 upkeep) – Although spell cost is still the same, cockatrices’s stone touch is no longer able to be triggered by magic ranged attack, so it loses combo with Focus Magic spell. Iron Skin (cost 21/105, 3 upkeep) – Change from rare to uncommon spell, research cost decreases from 4000 to 1400, and casting cost reduces from 24/120 to 21/105. Water Elemental (cost 40/-, 3 upkeep) – moved from sorcery as an uncommon nature combat summon, replacing the poor 'construct catapult'. The unit was appropriately adjusted with deal less damage, particularly its ranged attacks. While stats may appear underwhelming, this unit should not be underestimated in the hands of a smart player with the right set of support spells and under the right circumstances (and can also be a good desperate combat spell for a poorly defended city under siege). Crack's Call (cost 30/-) – Spell now calculates damage and burying chance differently and gives additional penalties to buried units. It now calculates chance to bury unit at 4% * unit armor chance, capped at 75%. A unit that is buried suffers -20% to defend in this mod. Burying a high-armor unit, rather than chance at damage, is more reliable and helps with defensive stalling. Damage is less dangerous in this mod, dealing 4 rolls of 25% chance at dealing 4 points of damage each (if unit is buried, two additional rolls take place) Transmute (cost -/60) – Research cost increases from 1920 to 2000. Great Lizard (cost -/200, 5 upkeep) – Given water walking (why wouldn't a great lizard swim?) and ability to blend in nature (stealth) as well as a few damage from poison attack.
PDF page 67 Nature Rare Spells Gaia’s Blessing (cost -/100, 3 upkeep) – Trade value increases. NEW: Transmute Equipment (cost -/90, 0 upkeep) – Rare. Pseudo unit enchantment that gives adamantium and orihalcon to a normal unit or grant permanent buff to a hero. There's a chance you may have many experienced units recruited before you transmuted minerals to adamantium – this is your chance to provide that to them. With this spell, you can permanently buff your heroes with similar value as what normal unit gains as well. Earthquake (cost -/150) – Still the same as in Caster of Magic for WIndows. Elemental Armor (cost 18/90, 1 upkeep) – Research cost reduces from 3200 to 3000, trade value is also reduced. NEW: Colossal Strength (cost 24/120, 3 upkeep) – Rare unit enchantment that increases melee and physical ranged strength by 40%. A new opportunity to buff heroes in nature and help make your single figure summons capable of damaging more units. Blizzard (cost -/120) – Trade value increases but attack strength reduces from 14 to 12 and research cost reduces from 4000 to 3500. NEW: Sacred Ancient (cost 32/-, 0 upkeep) – Uncommon combat summon. Immobile support units that grant +1 resist to all, have 'fairy dust' charges, and very high durability stats. This spell helps with defensive stalling, grants much-needed resistance, and grants nature a chance to use the otherwise-disabled 'fairy dust' when suitable multi-figure targets are your threat and randomly freeze them to skip a turn. This unit is disabled as rampaging monster. This immobile unit may be obtainable from the very rare global enchantment 'Fairy Ring'. If so, Sacred Ancient generates power income outside combat. Stone Giant (cost -/250, 5 upkeep) – lowered cost to 250 to ensure nature's summon superiority doesn't solely depend on its only rare-tier 'Survival Instinct'. Its impressive stats for the low cost make this a good spell adaptable to most situations. Abundance (cost -/150, 2 upkeep) – This enchantment is also additionally eliminated overfarming penalty from the city. Research cost increases from 3600 to 4000. Petrify (cost 20/-) – Research cost reduces from 4400 to 4000. NEW: Freezing Rain (cost 45/-) – At the end of each turn, each opponent's unit get hit by fairy dust-like attack. Units that do not have Cold Immunity, Non-Corporeal, or Immolation have a 50% chance to be frozen and fixed to the ground until the end of the next turn. NEW: Thunderbird (cost 350/7) - Rare. Giant eagle with strong lightning breath (activates only when attacking). The thunderbird is also immune to Hurricane (see below). This is the only relatively advanced flying unit offered by Nature. Earth Elemental (cost 50/-, 4 upkeep) – Spell is cheaper to research (5600 to 4600) but also reduces in trade value. Earth Elemental is now also get bonus based on resource of the combat tile on overland and what kind of terrain that Earth elemental summon upon in combat. Gorgons (cost -/320, 8 upkeep) – Slightly lower stats across the board, loses supernatural, and cheaper. Now this is the nature unit with 40 caster, shifted from behemoth. Gorgon is generally more usable after this change and can be optimized by having it cast petrify spell twice. This is also to ensure summon superiority of nature not being as dependent on rare-tier 'Survival Instinct' Survival Instinct (cost -/600, 15 upkeep) – For flavor, newly created normal units also gain small stat boosts based on city's surroundings: 'to defend' (+3% to +7%) based on gold-producing resources (which may be transmuted to mithril/adamantium otherwise).
PDF page 68 NEW: Hurricane (cost 30/-) – Rare, Reduces Ranged to Hit by 20% and breath to hit by 30% to all units including casting wizard. Eliminates flying to all units (except thunderbird and air elemental) including casting wizard's. Nature wizards are least vulnerable to these effects, especially wizards dominating with ground melee units, thus serving as a useful counter at a low cost against specific threats such as dragon units. Enemy AI is fairly smart when cast this spell to its advantage. Call The Wild – Nature Embrace (cost -/900, 30 upkeep) – In addition to the existing rampaging monster and lair guardian effects, all newly recruited units start with 'resist elements' if the recruiting town has an animist guild built. NEW: Ice Comet (cost 50/-) – Drop a gigantic ice comet at a target unit, This spell is acting as single target non- magical multifigure attack and also act as multi-target single turn freeze debuff too.
PDF page 69 Nature Very Rare or Higher Spells Clairvoyance (cost -/800, 20 upkeep) – Costlier but now also comes with an unrest quelling effect (2 rebels) to accommodate the higher population of 'abundance' cities and be able to more effectively protect against unrest- causing spells. Regeneration (cost 32/160, 5 upkeep) – Research cost reduces from 12000 to 8000. Fairy Ring (cost -/1200, 40 upkeep) – Now also grants 10 flat overland skill bonus plus 1 for every animist guild in towns controlled by casting wizard. Great Wyrm (cost -/450, 15 upkeep) – Reduced cost and given higher movement and water walking. NEW: Ice Age (cost -/1500, 100 upkeep) – This new global enchantment, replacing Earth Gate that move to Arcane, is Nature’s equivalent of Doomsday by causing climate change that causing changing in combat landscape, both land and sea, and reduce food production worldwide. As productive land gradually turns into tundra while once useless land of your empire turn into productive land. Additionally caster is coming into combat with free Freezing Rain and their nature creature gain cold immunity while all opponent sailing units losing 50% of movement points due to erratic wind pattern tha they could not handle. Herb Mastery (cost -/1000, 12 upkeep) - Herb Mastery has two added effects: it increases overall population growth of cities by +33% while halving pop reducing effects, a soft counter to Death realm. Nature has many tools to increase your maximum population capacity, but we need this to make it easier to reach those maximums. Call Lightning – Lightning Storm (cost 65/-) –lightning bolts are now strength 7 (60% hit chance) Behemoth (cost -/550, 14 upkeep) – Costlier and without caster 40, but given even higher offense and defense stats and abilities (e.g. armor piercing, cause fear) as well as a stoning gaze of -4 which helps unit hit flyers. It can also walk on water. Planetary Mastery (cost -/1000, 30 upkeep) – higher research cost and upkeep but now also doubles mineral bonuses to all cities (similar to Dwarf racial bonus), further establishing Nature realm as one dependent on the quality of your territory. Colossus (cost -/500, 15 upkeep) – Now has higher movement and +10% to defend, but lower ammo and higher cost. Entangle (cost 50/-) – still the same as in Caster of Magic for WIndows. Roots of Genesis (cost -/1200, 30 upkeep) – also has additional effect of spawning wild games in forest tiles and tundra tiles and nightshades in river tiles within city area of the caster at rate of 0.5% per tile. NEW: Gaia Mastery (reform, effect taken upon researched) – Increases enchantment dispel resistance, reduces casting cost of the spells, and buff creature of the Nature realm under wizard control. This reform is only available to Specialist retort holder with Nature as primary realm. Once this spell appears on research page, it will exclude chance to get mastery of other realm. NEW: Lesser Gaia Lord (cost -/777, 20 upkeep) – This spell could only be learned with Conjuring Pact and 10 Nature spell books. NEW: Great Gaia Lord (cost -/999, 30 upkeep) – This spell could only be learned with Conjuring Pact and 12 Nature spell books. NEW: Power of Nature (cost 77/-) – This spell could only be learned by Enchanter wizard who already have access to Resist Elements, Water Walking, Nature Link, Venom, Colossal Strength, Elemental Armor, Iron Skin, and Regeneration. This spell would allow the Enchanter to cast all above unit enchantment all at once on single target!
PDF page 70 NEW: Force of Nature (cost 150/-) – This spell could only be learned by Runemaster wizard who already have access to Lightning Storm, Entangle, Freezing Rain, and Hurricane. This spell would allow the Runemaster to cast all above combat enchantment all at once!
PDF page 71 Sorcery: Sorcery realm specializes in utility spells, negating enemy magic, and illusionist trickery. It rewards opportunistic players. The realm has several means of expanding your abilities as a wizard, whether it is power income, casting skill, gold. Many spells act as a reaction of a situation, often to shut down threats or bring gameplay mechanics in your favor: ground troops threatening your city? Hold them in place or make your city fly! A spell threatens your game? Counter or dispel it! Don't want to lose a unit or a city to spells in a game revolving around magic? Make them universally immune! At its most powerful, Sorcery can stop time itself. These are generally defensive tools for cautious wizards. The Sorcery school of magic also carries naval advantages with this mod's new spells. The dispelling nature of Sorcery also applies to banishing creatures altogether. Meanwhile, sorcery summoners have a wide variety of highly strategic combat and overland summons and thus are good candidates for Conjurer retort. New spells further establish these realm characteristics. Removed Sorcery Spells Old Seravy Version of Power Link is removed due to its capabilities to break entire game is it is coming early with several wizards still active. Great Unsummoning is removed due to it cause end turn exceptionally long during its processing of result. Sorcery Common Spells Floating Island (cost -/45, 1 upkeep) – the spell is the same as in Caster of Magic but the unit able to be upgraded upon summon by later Mariner Mastery. Guardian Wind (cost 6/30, 1 upkeep) – trading value is increased from 6 to 7. AEther Spark (cost 12/-) – attack strength change from 20 at 30% hit chance to 10 at 60% hit chance and research cost decreases from 260 to 240. Nagas (cost -/65, 1 upkeep) – reduced in cost and upkeep to slightly improve early sorcery game on this front relative to other realms, but overall stats decreased (-1 melee, -1hp). Nagas (amphibious) gain faster movement and fire immunity while fighting in an ocean tile. Phantom Warriors (cost -/65, 1 upkeep) – research cost decreases from 320 to 280. Vertigo (cost 10/-) – the spell change to common level and reduction in trade value (from 15 to 11) as well as research cost (from 640 to 280) to common level.
